name: ABCSG-16 (SALSA)
population: Postmenopausal HR+ who already completed 5 yr adjuvant ET. Median age 64. T1 73%, N0 67%. 71% no chemo.
treatment: Extended anastrozole 2 more yr (total 7) vs 5 more yr (total 10)
endpoints: ⚠️ Clinical fracture HR 1.35 (1.00–1.84) — favours shorter arm
takeaway: 5 extra yr of anastrozole is no better than 2 after an initial 5 yr of ET — and costs more fractures. Shorter extension is enough.

name: ACOSOG Z1031
population: Postmenopausal, ER+, clinical stage II–III (>2 cm; T2–T4c, N0–3), regardless of HER2.
treatment: Neoadjuvant exemestane vs letrozole vs anastrozole × 16–18 wk
endpoints: Luminal A → PEPI-0 27.1% vs Luminal B 10.7%, P=0.004
takeaway: All three AIs perform alike as neoadjuvant ET; big breast-conservation gain (68%). Luminal A responds far better than Luminal B.

name: ACTS-GC
population: Japanese, stage II/IIIa/IIIb (T1 excluded), after R0 gastrectomy + D2 lymphadenectomy.
treatment: S-1 (TS-1) × 1 year vs surgery alone
takeaway: 1 year of adjuvant S-1 after D2 resection improves both RFS and OS in Asian gastric cancer. S-1 alone is under-powered for stage III/N2.

name: ADAURA
population: Completely resected EGFR Ex19del/L858R NSCLC, stage IB–IIIA (AJCC 7th), ECOG 0–1. Adjuvant chemo allowed pre-randomisation (60%).
treatment: Osimertinib up to 3 yr vs placebo
takeaway: 3 years of adjuvant osimertinib in resected EGFR-mutant stage IB–IIIA NSCLC delivers both DFS and OS benefit, with striking CNS protection.

name: AEGEAN
population: Resectable stage IIA–IIIB (N2) NSCLC (AJCC 8th), no EGFR/ALK alterations, ECOG 0–1.
treatment: Perioperative durvalumab + chemo vs placebo + chemo; adjuvant durvalumab × 1 yr (durvalumab 1500 mg + chemo Q3W × 4; surgery within 6 wk)
endpoints: ✅ 1st interim: mEFS NR vs 25.9 mo (1-yr 73.4% vs 64.5%) — HR 0.68 (0.53–0.88), P=0.004. 2nd interim (median f/u 25.9 mo): mEFS NR vs 30.0 mo (3-yr 60.1% vs 47.9%) — HR 0.69 (0.55–0.88)
⚠️ HR 0.66 (0.47–0.92); numerically favors durvalumab but P=0.0137 > 0.0123 → NS
⚠️ mOS NR vs 53.2 mo — HR 0.89 (0.70–1.14); not formally tested
takeaway: Perioperative durvalumab plus chemotherapy improved both pCR and EFS over chemotherapy alone in resectable NSCLC. OS was not significant, and 17% of placebo patients received ICI after progression.

name: ALASCCA
population: Radically resected PI3K-pathway–altered CRC — stage II–III colon, stage I–III rectum. Median age 66, 52% female, 33% rectal. Grp A = PIK3CA exon 9/20 hotspot; Grp B = other PIK3CA/PIK3R1/PTEN variants.
treatment: Aspirin 160 mg daily × 3 yr vs placebo, started ≤12 wk after R0 resection
takeaway: Cheap, repurposed aspirin halves recurrence in PI3K-altered resected CRC — and the benefit extends past PIK3CA hotspots to PIK3R1/PTEN (~37% of all CRC eligible). Largest effect in rectal cancer and in women.

name: ALINA
population: Completely resected ALK+ NSCLC, stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA (AJCC 7th), ECOG 0–1, no prior systemic therapy.
treatment: Alectinib 600 mg BID × 2 yr vs platinum chemo × 4 cycles
takeaway: Chemo-free adjuvant alectinib × 2 yr is now SOC for resected ALK+ NSCLC — dramatic DFS and CNS benefit; OS immature.

name: AMBASSADOR
population: Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma — pT2–T4 after neoadjuvant chemo, or pT3–T4 without.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs observation
takeaway: Adjuvant pembrolizumab doubles DFS in MIBC but shows no OS gain — likely confounded by crossover to adjuvant/salvage nivolumab.

name: APHINITY
population: HER2+ EBC, node-positive (63%) or high-risk node-negative (tumour >1 cm).
treatment: Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + chemo (1 yr dual anti-HER2) vs placebo + trastuzumab + chemo
takeaway: Adding 1 yr of pertuzumab is SOC only for node-positive HER2+ EBC. High-risk node-negative gains nothing; OS shows a trend but never reaches significance.

name: ARTIST
population: Korean, ECOG 0–1, stage IB–IIIB/IV M0, after R0 resection + D2.
treatment: Capecitabine/cisplatin (XP) + RT vs XP alone
endpoints: ✅ N+ 3-yr DFS 76% vs 72%, P=0.04; ✅ intestinal type 94% vs 83%, P=0.01
takeaway: After a proper D2 resection, adding RT to adjuvant chemo helps locoregional control but not survival — except in node-positive and intestinal-type subgroups.

name: ARTIST 2
population: Korean, ECOG 0–1, stage IIA–IIIC, node-positive, after R0 + D2.
treatment: SOX vs SOX + RT vs S-1 alone
takeaway: Doublet SOX beats single-agent S-1 after D2 resection; adding radiotherapy on top of D2 + doublet is redundant.

name: ASTRRA
population: Premenopausal (age ≤45; 58% aged 40–45), ER+, post-surgery + (neo)adjuvant chemo, who remained premenopausal or regained ovarian function within 2 yr of chemo.
treatment: Tamoxifen 5 yr + ovarian function suppression 2 yr vs tamoxifen alone 5 yr
takeaway: Just 2 years of added OFS buys a durable 8-year DFS benefit, greatest at age 40–45 (HR 0.50). Under 40 saw no gain — suggesting they need the full 5 years of OFS.

name: ATAC
population: Postmenopausal after surgery ± RT ± chemo. Mean age 64. HR status unrestricted but 84% HR+ (the analysis focus).
treatment: Anastrozole 1 mg/d vs tamoxifen 20 mg/d × 5 yr
takeaway: 5 yr of upfront anastrozole beats tamoxifen on DFS but not OS, with a real carryover effect after stopping. Early ET side effects at 3 months predicted lower recurrence in both arms.

name: ATLAS
population: Women already several years into tamoxifen, uncertain whether to stop. Age, HR/nodal status unrestricted. Main efficacy population ER+ (n=6,846).
treatment: Extended tamoxifen — continue to 10 yr vs stop at 5 yr
endpoints: ❌ Endometrial CA RR 1.74, PE RR 1.87 — no net excess non-BC mortality
takeaway: 10 years of tamoxifen beats 5 on both recurrence and survival, and the benefit is strongly time-delayed — it roughly halves breast-cancer mortality in the second decade after diagnosis.

name: ATOMIC
population: R0-resected stage III colon cancer (any T, N1–2, M0), dMMR/MSI-H, ECOG 0–2. 54% high-risk (T4, N2 or both).
treatment: Atezolizumab + mFOLFOX6 vs mFOLFOX6 alone (6 months)
endpoints: ⚠️ 5-yr 89.7% vs 87.9% — HR 0.90 (0.55–1.47), NS at first analysis
takeaway: Adding atezolizumab to adjuvant FOLFOX halves recurrence risk in resected stage III dMMR colon cancer. OS not yet separated.

name: AVANT
population: Stage III or high-risk stage II colon cancer after resection.
treatment: Adjuvant FOLFOX4 vs bevacizumab-FOLFOX4 vs bevacizumab-XELOX × 6 months
takeaway: Bevacizumab added to adjuvant chemo made outcomes worse, not better — a definitive negative trial. Not recommended.

name: AZUR-2
population: Not yet reported.
treatment: Perioperative dostarlimab
takeaway: Ongoing phase III of perioperative dostarlimab in colorectal cancer. Watch this space.

name: BCIRG-006
population: HER2+, node-positive or high-risk node-negative (T1–T3). ER/PR+ ≈54%.
treatment: 3 arms — AC-T (control) vs AC-T + trastuzumab vs TCH (non-anthracycline). Trastuzumab × 1 yr
endpoints: ✅ AC-T+H 84% vs TCH 81% vs AC-T 75% — HR 0.64 (P<0.001) and 0.75 (P=0.04) vs AC-T
No significant difference between the two trastuzumab arms
takeaway: Adjuvant trastuzumab × 1 yr improves DFS and OS. The anthracycline-free TCH regimen matches it with less cardiotoxicity — a better risk–benefit profile.

name: BIG 1-98
population: Postmenopausal ER+ after surgery. Median age 61, 57% node-positive, 25% prior chemo, 39% prior HRT.
treatment: Letrozole 2.5 mg/d vs tamoxifen 20 mg/d × 5 yr (4-arm design incl. sequences; core analysis pools letrozole-initial vs tamoxifen-initial)
endpoints: ❌ 166 vs 192 deaths — NS (median FU only 25.8 mo)
takeaway: 5 yr of upfront letrozole beats tamoxifen on DFS, driven mainly by fewer distant recurrences. Note the subgroup pattern is the opposite of ATAC — benefit was greatest in node-positive, chemo-treated women.

name: Cercek et al (dostarlimab rectal)
population: dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer — stage II 1/14, stage III 13/14. Lynch syndrome 57%.
treatment: Dostarlimab (anti–PD-1) Q3W × 6 months
takeaway: Every single dMMR rectal cancer patient achieved a clinical complete response on PD-1 blockade alone. Surgery and radiation can be omitted entirely under watch-and-wait — a landmark, if tiny, result.

name: CLASSIC
population: South Korea/China/Taiwan, stage II–IIIB, after R0 + D2 resection.
treatment: CAPOX (capecitabine + oxaliplatin) vs surgery alone
takeaway: Adjuvant CAPOX after D2 resection improves DFS and OS — and unlike S-1 alone, the benefit holds up in advanced stage and node-positive disease.

name: CheckMate-274
population: Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma — pT2–T4 after neoadjuvant chemo, or pT3–T4 without.
treatment: Nivolumab vs placebo
takeaway: First FDA-approved adjuvant ICI in MIBC. Benefit is richest in PD-L1-positive patients and those who had cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemo.

name: CheckMate-577
population: R0 stage II–III esophageal/GEJ cancer after neoadjuvant chemoradiation with residual disease (non-pCR). Adeno 71% / SCC 29%; ≥ypN1 58%; TC ≥1% only 16%.
treatment: Nivolumab × 1 yr vs placebo (2:1), no crossover
endpoints: ✅ SCC 29.7 vs 11.0 mo (HR 0.61); adeno 19.4 vs 11.1 mo (HR 0.75)
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab doubles DFS and is now SOC — but only for patients with residual disease after CRT. Benefit is greatest in squamous histology; no OS signal yet.

name: CheckMate-77T
population: Resectable stage IIA (>4 cm)–IIIB NSCLC (AJCC 8th), no EGFR/ALK alterations, ECOG 0–1.
treatment: Perioperative nivolumab + chemo vs placebo + chemo; adjuvant × 1 yr (nivolumab 360 mg + chemo × 4; surgery within 6 wk)
takeaway: Perioperative nivolumab plus chemotherapy improved pCR and EFS over chemotherapy alone in resectable NSCLC, with OS still maturing. Post hoc, patients without pCR and PD-L1-negative patients appeared to benefit from adjuvant nivolumab.

name: CheckMate-816
population: Resectable stage IB–IIIA NSCLC (AJCC 7th), no EGFR/ALK alterations, ECOG 0–1.
treatment: Neoadjuvant nivolumab 360 mg + chemotherapy q3w ×3 vs chemotherapy alone; surgery within 6 wks, no adjuvant nivolumab
takeaway: Neoadjuvant nivolumab + chemotherapy improved EFS and OS over neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone, shifting ICI use from the adjuvant to the neoadjuvant setting. The OS benefit was not significant in PD-L1-negative patients.

name: CONTINUUM
population: Newly diagnosed non-metastatic high-risk locoregionally advanced NPC, stage III–IVa (AJCC 8th), excluding T3–4N0 and T3N1. Age 18–65. Definitive chemoradiation, non-surgical.
treatment: Sintilimab + GP induction → cisplatin CCRT vs GP induction → CCRT alone
endpoints: ❌ Not reached, no difference at 41.9-mo median FU
takeaway: First phase III showing PD-1 blockade across induction, concurrent and adjuvant phases improves EFS in high-risk LANPC (~10% absolute gain at 3 yr). No OS benefit yet — plausibly because 64% of controls got PD-1 blockade after progression.

name: CTNeoBC (pooled analysis)
population: Pooled 12 neoadjuvant trials of high-risk EBC. T2 61%, cN+ 46%, HR+ 83%, HER2+ 17%, TNBC 30%.
treatment: Anthracycline- and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemo ± trastuzumab
endpoints: ypT0/is ypN0 ~18%. TNBC 33.6%; HER2+/HR− + trastuzumab 50.3%; HR+/HER2− G1-2 7.5%
HR 0.48 (0.43–0.54); best in TNBC HR 0.24 and HER2+/HR− HR 0.15
❌ Trial-level R² = 0.03 (EFS), 0.24 (OS) — pCR NOT a validated trial-level surrogate
takeaway: pCR strongly predicts an individual patient's outcome — especially in TNBC and HER2+/HR− — but fails as a trial-level surrogate. This analysis fixed the pCR definition as ypT0/is ypN0 and underpinned FDA's 2014 accelerated-approval guidance.

name: DeCIDE
population: N2 or N3 non-metastatic SCCHN, treatment-naive, KPS ≥70. Oropharynx 58%, stage IVa 86%, N3 11%, T3–T4 45%.
treatment: Induction TPF ×2 → DFHX chemoradiation vs DFHX chemoradiation alone
endpoints: ✅ Distant recurrence without prior locoregional failure P=0.043 (nominal)
⚠️ SAE 47% vs 28%, plus 4 toxic deaths during induction
takeaway: Induction TPF added nothing on top of an effective chemoradiation backbone. The only signal — fewer isolated distant recurrences — is hypothesis-generating. The trial was underpowered (280 vs 400 planned, 56% power).

name: DESTINY-Breast05
population: HER2+ EBC with residual disease (non-pCR in breast or nodes) after neoadjuvant taxane + anti-HER2. Inoperable at baseline 50%, node-positive 80%, dual anti-HER2 70%.
treatment: Adjuvant T-DXd vs T-DM1 for residual disease
takeaway: T-DXd clearly outperforms T-DM1 for residual HER2+ disease after neoadjuvant therapy, including HER2 2+/ISH+. Watch for ILD.

name: DESTINY-Breast11
population: High-risk HER2+ early breast cancer (≥cT3 cN0, or cT0–4 cN1–3), ECOG 0–1. HR-negative capped at 30%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant T-DXd ×4 → THP ×4 vs ddAC ×4 → THP ×4 (T-DXd ×8 monotherapy arm closed early)
takeaway: First phase III to establish an anthracycline- and carboplatin-free neoadjuvant regimen in high-risk HER2+ disease, with an 11-point pCR gain. EFS still immature.

name: DIPPER
population: T4N1M0 or T1–4N2–3M0 NPC (AJCC 8th) who completed GP induction + cisplatin CCRT. Age 18–65, ECOG 0–1, randomised within 2 wk of last radiation dose.
treatment: Adjuvant camrelizumab 200 mg q3w × 12 cycles vs observation
takeaway: Adjuvant-only PD-1 blockade after definitive IC-CCRT buys the same ~10% EFS gain as CONTINUUM with markedly less toxicity and no QoL hit. Supports adjuvant sequencing as the lower-toxicity way to deliver ICI in high-risk LANPC.

name: ExteNET
population: HER2+ stage 1–3 (amended to stage 2–3) who completed neo/adjuvant trastuzumab ≤1 yr earlier.
treatment: Neratinib × 1 yr maintenance vs placebo
takeaway: A year of maintenance neratinib improves iDFS, with benefit concentrated in HR+ disease. Severe diarrhoea is the limiting toxicity.

name: FLOT4
population: German, ECOG 0–1, gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma stage ≥cT2 or node-positive.
treatment: FLOT ×4 pre + ×4 post vs ECF/ECX ×3 pre + ×3 post
takeaway: FLOT beats ECF/ECX on every axis — OS, DFS, R0 rate and pCR. The perioperative standard for gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma.

name: FNCLCC-FFCD
population: French, ECOG 0–1, all stages except CIS. Predominantly GEJ tumours. R0 rate 84% (chemo) vs 74% (surgery alone).
treatment: Cisplatin/5-FU ×3 pre + ×4 post vs surgery alone
takeaway: Perioperative cisplatin/5-FU improves survival even in a GEJ-heavy population — a European companion to MAGIC.

name: FOxTROT
population: CT-staged T3–4, N0–2 colon cancer with extramural extension ≥5 mm (≥1 mm after pilot). Median age 63; cT4 25%; cN+ 75%.
treatment: 6 wk neoadjuvant mFOLFOX/CAPOX → surgery → 18 wk adjuvant chemo, vs 24 wk adjuvant chemo (2:1) ± panitumumab in RAS-wt
endpoints: Complete 4% vs 0%; any regression 66% vs 18%; R0 94% vs 89%
❌ Colon-cancer death RR 0.74, all-cause RR 0.76 — both NS
takeaway: First phase III of neoadjuvant chemo in colon cancer — fewer 2-yr recurrences, more R0, more downstaging. dMMR tumours get nothing from it (they need immunotherapy instead).

name: GEICAM/2006-03
population: Operable luminal breast cancer (ER+/PR+/HER2−). Premenopausal ~53%, T2 ~74%, N0 55%, Ki67 ≤10% in 42%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant chemo (EC ×4 → docetaxel ×4) vs endocrine therapy (exemestane ± goserelin) × 24 wk
endpoints: ~2% (1 patient) vs 0 — near-zero in both arms
High Ki67 >10%: 67% (ChT) vs 42% (ET); Low Ki67: 63% vs 58% — comparable
takeaway: In luminal early breast cancer, chemo only outperforms endocrine therapy when Ki67 is high. Low-Ki67 (luminal A) tumours respond equally to ET and may safely skip chemo.

name: GORTEC 2007-02
population: Non-metastatic, non-operated stage III–IV SCC of oral cavity, oro/hypopharynx or larynx with bulky nodal disease (N2b, N2c or N3); age 18–80, ECOG 0–1. T4 49%, N2c–N3 75%, oropharynx 64%; p16-negative 74% of tested OPC; smokers 90%.
treatment: Induction TPF ×3 → cetuximab-RT vs concurrent carboplatin + 5-FU + RT (CT-RT)
endpoints: ❌ Not met — 2-yr 36% vs 38%, HR 0.93 (0.73–1.20), P=.58 (powered for HR 0.66); p16+ HR 0.78, p16− HR 1.28, interaction P=.35
⚠️ HR 1.12 (0.86–1.46), P=.39 — numerically favors CT-RT; no difference regardless of p16 status
takeaway: The primary endpoint was not met: induction TPF → cetuximab-RT did not improve 2-yr PFS (36% vs 38%) versus standard concurrent chemoRT in N2b–N3 disease, with no benefit in locoregional control or OS and no interaction with p16 status. The one reproducible signal was fewer distant metastases (HR 0.54), concordant with DeCIDE and MACH-NC. Against that, TPF-related mortality was 6.6% and febrile neutropenia 17% (possibly unacceptable in this smoking/alcohol-related population), and 17% of the induction arm never received curative RT; unlike DeCIDE/PARADIGM, this trial met its accrual target.

name: HERA
population: HER2+ EBC after surgery + ≥4 cycles (neo)adjuvant chemo ± RT; node-positive (any) or node-negative if >1 cm.
treatment: Adjuvant trastuzumab 1 yr vs 2 yr vs observation
endpoints: ❌ HR 1.02 (0.89–1.17) — no added benefit, more cardiotoxicity
takeaway: Established 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab as the standard. Doubling to 2 years adds only cardiotoxicity.

name: IDEAL
population: Postmenopausal who completed 5 yr of any adjuvant ET — but ~88% had prior AI exposure (unlike MA.17). pN1 47.5%, 68% prior chemo.
treatment: Extended letrozole 2.5 yr vs 5 yr (open-label, up-front randomisation)
endpoints: ❌ 104 vs 96 deaths — HR 1.04 (0.78–1.38), numerically favours shorter arm
takeaway: 5 extra yr of letrozole is no better than 2.5 — except for preventing second primary breast cancers. Caveats: open-label, ~30% attrition before the arms diverge, and only 60% total compliance.

name: IES
population: Postmenopausal, disease-free after 2–3 yr of adjuvant tamoxifen (median 2.4 yr). Mean age 64, 44% node-positive, 33% prior chemo.
treatment: Switch strategy — switch to exemestane vs continue tamoxifen, to 5 yr total ET
endpoints: ✅ TTDR HR 0.84 (0.74–0.96) — gap entirely in bone sites; non-bone identical
⚠️ TTDR after 2.5 yr HR 0.94 (0.80–1.10) — no carryover effect
takeaway: After 2–3 years of tamoxifen, switching to exemestane beats completing 5 years of tamoxifen on DFS but not OS. Unlike ATAC, there is no carryover once treatment stops.

name: IMpassion031
population: Untreated stage II–III TNBC; cT2–T4, cN0–N3, centrally confirmed triple-negative. PD-L1 unselected (SP142 IC ≥1% = positive, 46% positive). ECOG 0–1, node+ 38%, median age 51.
treatment: Neoadjuvant atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel → AC vs placebo + chemo; atezolizumab arm continued adjuvant atezo ×11
endpoints: ⚠️ 69% vs 49% (Δ20%), P=0.021 — boundary α=0.0184 NOT crossed
takeaway: Atezolizumab raises pCR in early TNBC regardless of PD-L1 status — but the PD-L1+ co-primary formally missed, and the time-to-event endpoints were never mature, so it never became practice-changing the way KEYNOTE-522 did. The anthracycline backbone may matter: AC-free NeoTRIPaPDL1 was negative.

name: IMpower010
population: Completely resected NSCLC, stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA (AJCC 7th), ECOG 0–1, after 1–4 cycles adjuvant platinum chemo.
treatment: Atezolizumab ×16 cycles (~1 yr) vs best supportive care; no crossover
takeaway: Benefit is concentrated in stage II–IIIA with high PD-L1 (TC ≥50%, especially EGFR/ALK wild-type). ITT DFS never reached significance → FDA approval limited to stage II–IIIA, PD-L1 ≥1%.

name: IMvoke010
population: High-risk locally advanced SCCHN with no progression after definitive therapy. Stage IVa/IVb p16− or stage III p16+ (18%). Required ≥2 treatment modalities; CR to prior therapy 84%; no primary surgery 62%; PD-L1 TAP ≥5% ~80%.
treatment: Adjuvant atezolizumab 1200 mg q3w × 1 yr vs placebo after definitive therapy; no crossover
takeaway: Adjuvant atezolizumab after definitive therapy failed on EFS and OS. Only PD-L1 TAP ≥5% showed a numerical trend; a longer interval between RT and ICI may matter.

name: INT-0116 (Macdonald)
population: Predominantly Caucasian, ECOG 0–2, stage ≥IB/M0 after resection. Only 10% had a D2 lymphadenectomy.
treatment: 5-FU/leucovorin + radiotherapy vs surgery alone
takeaway: The first trial proving adjuvant therapy helps in gastric cancer — but because D2 dissection was rare, adjuvant chemoradiation is best read as compensating for inadequate surgery. Consider RT when the resection was not D2.

name: JACCRO GC-07
population: Japanese, ECOG 0–1, stage IIIA/IIIB/IIIC after R0 + D2 resection.
treatment: Docetaxel + S-1 (DS-1) vs S-1 alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to S-1 improves RFS and OS in stage III gastric cancer at the cost of more toxicity. Oddly, stage IIIB alone showed no survival benefit.

name: KATHERINE
population: HER2+ early breast cancer with residual disease (non-pCR in breast/LN) after neoadjuvant taxane chemotherapy + trastuzumab with or without pertuzumab. Inoperable 20%, node-positive 45%, dual-HER2 20%.
treatment: Adjuvant T-DM1 vs trastuzumab after neoadjuvant therapy for residual disease
endpoints: ✅ 89.1% vs 84.4% (Δ4.7 pp) — HR 0.66 (0.51–0.87), P=0.003 (crossed O'Brien-Fleming boundary)
takeaway: In HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant trastuzumab-taxane chemotherapy, escalating to adjuvant T-DM1 improved iDFS and OS and became standard of care. The benefit held regardless of neoadjuvant pertuzumab.

name: KEYNOTE-412
population: High-risk unresected locally advanced HNSCC requiring definitive CRT (oropharynx 50%, larynx 22%, hypopharynx 18%, oral cavity 10%; oral cavity had to be unresected). p16+ 26%; stage IV 66%; T3–T4 83–86%; CPS ≥1 ~85%, ≥20 ~36%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (1 cycle → 2 cycles + CCRT → 14 adjuvant) + cisplatin 100 mg/m² q3w CCRT vs placebo + CCRT
endpoints: ❌ Not met — median NR vs 46.6 mo; 24-mo 63% vs 56% — HR 0.83 (0.68–1.03), log-rank P=0.043 (threshold P≤0.024, NS)
takeaway: This was the third negative concurrent ICI-(C)RT trial that failed both EFS and OS. The CPS ≥1 subgroup came closest to an EFS benefit (HR 0.80), in contrast with the neoadjuvant KEYNOTE-689.

name: KEYNOTE-522
population: TNBC; T1c N1–2 or T2–4 N0–2 (AJCC 7th), stage II–III. PD-L1 unselected (CPS ≥1 in 83%); N+ 52%; stage III 25%.
treatment: Perioperative pembrolizumab + chemo → adjuvant pembrolizumab ×9 vs matching placebo; chemo: TCarbo ×4 → AC or EC ×4
takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab + chemo improved pCR, EFS and OS in stage II–III TNBC and is the standard. The benefit held regardless of PD-L1, unlike metastatic KEYNOTE-355 where benefit was seen only with CPS ≥10.

name: KEYNOTE-671
population: Resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC (AJCC 8th); molecularly unselected (targetable ~6%); ECOG 0–1.
treatment: Perioperative pembrolizumab 200 mg + chemo Q3W ×4 → surgery within 20 weeks → adjuvant pembrolizumab 1 yr, vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: ✅ Median NR vs. 52.4 m — HR 0.72 (0.56–0.93), significant; 3-yr 71% vs. 64%
takeaway: The first perioperative ICI + chemo regimen to show EFS, OS and pCR benefit in resectable NSCLC. pCR/mPR predict survival, and patients with TPS <1% benefited less.

name: KEYNOTE-689
population: Resectable LA-HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx/larynx; p16+ stage III, other stage III–IVA). Oral cavity 60% (mostly OP candidate); HPV− ~95%; CPS ≥10 ~65%, CPS ≥1 ~95%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w ×2 → surgery → pembro ×3 with RT/CRT → pembro ×12 vs surgery → RT/CRT
endpoints: ✅ pCR 4.3% vs 0% (CPS ≥10), 3.2% vs 0% (CPS ≥1), 3.0% vs 0% (total); mPR 13.7% vs 0%, 9.8% vs 0%, 9.4% vs 0%; all P<0.001. No pathological response in any CPS <1 patient

⚠️ Numerically favored but not significant. 3-yr OS CPS ≥10 68.2% vs 59.2% — HR 0.72 (0.52–0.98), P=0.04 (boundary 0.0104 not crossed); CPS ≥1 69.0% vs 60.2% — HR 0.72 (0.56–0.94); total 68.4% vs 61.1% — HR 0.76 (0.59–0.98), not formally tested
takeaway: First positive peri-operative ICI trial in locally advanced HNSCC, with an EFS benefit driven by fewer distant relapses and no operation delay (R0 88.4% vs 87.7%). Caveats: OS is immature, and FDA approval is only in CPS ≥1.

name: KEYNOTE-905 / EV-303
population: Cisplatin-INELIGIBLE muscle-invasive bladder cancer, relatively advanced disease.
treatment: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (perioperative) vs surgery alone
takeaway: EV + pembrolizumab transforms outcomes in cisplatin-ineligible MIBC — pCR, EFS and OS all dramatically positive. Note the control arm received no chemotherapy at all, which flatters the comparison.

name: KRISTINE
population: HER2+ stage II–III breast cancer (>2 cm), ECOG 0–1, LVEF ≥55%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant T-DM1 + pertuzumab vs TCHP; adjuvant ×12 cycles of T-DM1+P vs HP
takeaway: De-escalating to chemo-free T-DM1 + pertuzumab was worse than TCHP on pCR and markedly worse on EFS. TCHP remains the neoadjuvant standard.

name: Ludford et al (neoadjuvant pembrolizumab, dMMR)
population: dMMR/MSI-H solid tumours — CRC 27 (colon 19, rectal 8), non-CRC 8. Stage II 8, stage III 26. Unresectable 26%. Lynch syndrome 46%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab Q3W × 6 months
endpoints: ✅ 65% of all resected; 79% of resected CRC
takeaway: Confirms the extraordinary sensitivity of dMMR tumours to PD-1 blockade beyond rectal cancer. Non-operative management (1 yr pembrolizumab + surveillance) was feasible; an early ctDNA drop predicted benefit.

name: MA.17
population: Postmenopausal ER+ who completed 4.5–6 yr of adjuvant tamoxifen. Median age 62, 46% node-positive, 45% prior chemo.
treatment: Extended letrozole 2.5 mg/d vs placebo × 5 yr after tamoxifen. Stopped early at first interim analysis (2.4 yr) for efficacy
takeaway: Extended letrozole after 5 years of tamoxifen improves DFS, with an OS benefit confined to node-positive disease. Two caveats: the DFS definition excludes deaths, and crossover was allowed at 2.5 yr so the planned 5-year comparison never happened.

name: MA.17R
population: Postmenopausal, disease-free after 4.5–6 yr of any AI (preceded by tamoxifen in most). Median age 65, median 10.6 yr since diagnosis. T1–T2 90%, N0 47%/N1 48%.
treatment: Extended letrozole × 5 further years vs placebo — AI following AI, out to 10 yr
endpoints: ✅ 1.4% vs 3.2% — HR 0.42 (0.22–0.81), P=0.007, the most robust finding
❌ Exactly 100 deaths in each arm — HR 0.97 (0.73–1.28), P=0.83
takeaway: 10 years of AI beats 5 on DFS and contralateral breast cancer, with zero OS benefit and more cardiovascular deaths. The primary endpoint censors deaths — count them and the effect drops to borderline.

name: MAGIC
population: European, ECOG 0–1, stage ≥II gastric/GEJ. D2 in only ~30%, R0 ~70%.
treatment: ECF ×3 pre + ×3 post vs surgery alone
takeaway: The first perioperative chemotherapy trial in gastric cancer to show an OS benefit — established the perioperative paradigm later improved on by FLOT4.

name: MATTERHORN
population: Global (Asian-enriched), ECOG 0–1, stage II/III/IVA gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (30% GEJ).
treatment: Durvalumab + FLOT vs FLOT alone
takeaway: Perioperative durvalumab + FLOT improves pCR, EFS and OS — a new standard, though the Asian-enriched population raises questions about generalisability.

name: MINDACT
population: Women 18–70, initially node-negative then N1 allowed (79% N0, 21% N1). Median age 55; 88% HR+, 9.5% HER2+, 9.6% TNBC. The key group — high clinical/low genomic risk — was genuinely high-risk: 48% node+, 93% grade 2–3.
treatment: MammaPrint 70-gene signature; chemo vs no chemo randomised only in the two discordant-risk groups
endpoints: ✅ High clinical/low genomic, no chemo: 94.7% (95% CI 92.5–96.2) — lower bound >92%, non-inferiority met
✅ 93.3% vs 90.3% — HR 0.64 (0.43–0.95), P=0.03 (the only nominally significant difference)
⚠️ DMFS HR 1.17 (0.59–2.28) — chemo does not help
⚠️ No significant difference in either discordant group
takeaway: Genomic testing spares chemotherapy in 46% of clinically high-risk women. But there is no point testing clinically low-risk patients — whatever the genomic score, they don't need chemo.

name: monarchE
population: HR+/HER2−, NODE-POSITIVE, high-risk EBC. Cohort 1 (91%): pN2, or pN1 with grade 3 or cT3. Cohort 2 (9%): pN1, grade 1–2, Ki-67 ≥20%. Median age 51, ~60% had ≥4 nodes, ~74% stage III, 95% prior chemo, 44% premenopausal. Node-negative excluded.
treatment: Abemaciclib × 2 yr + endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone
endpoints: ⭐ Benefit DEEPENS after the drug stops: Δ2.8% (2 yr) → 4.8% (3 yr) → 6.4% (4 yr)
✅ HR 0.659 (0.567–0.767) — 71% of iDFS events were distant metastases
takeaway: The first CDK4/6 inhibitor to work in the adjuvant setting — cuts iDFS events by 34% in high-risk node-positive disease, and the benefit keeps widening after the 2 years of treatment end.

name: MOSAIC
population: Resected stage II (40%) or stage III (60%) colon cancer. Rectal cancer excluded.
treatment: Adjuvant FOLFOX4 vs 5-FU/leucovorin × 6 months
takeaway: Established oxaliplatin in the adjuvant setting — DFS benefit concentrated in stage III; OS did not separate at 3 years.

name: NATALEE
population: HR+/HER2−, stage II or III — deliberately BROAD, and unlike monarchE it includes NODE-NEGATIVE disease. Median age 52; 59.6% stage III; 15.6% pN0; 88% prior chemo; 44% premenopausal.
treatment: Ribociclib 400 mg/d × 3 yr + NSAI vs NSAI alone × 5 yr. All men and premenopausal women got OFS. Note 400 mg, not the 600 mg of MONALEESA — chosen to make 3 years tolerable
endpoints: ✅ Stage II HR 0.700; stage III HR 0.755
takeaway: Extends adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition to a much broader population than monarchE — stage II–III including selected node-negative disease, which monarchE excluded entirely. Lower dose, longer duration.

name: NEOADAURA
population: Not yet entered in your database.
treatment: Neoadjuvant osimertinib (EGFR TKI)
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — no data captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder entry in your Notion DB — worth filling in with the neoadjuvant osimertinib results.

name: NeoSphere
population: HER2+ breast cancer — operable (T2–3 N0–1), locally advanced, or inflammatory (T4d); primary tumour >2 cm. ER+ ~48%, operable ~61%.
treatment: 4 arms — A: trastuzumab + docetaxel; B: docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (TPH); C: trastuzumab + pertuzumab (chemo-free); D: docetaxel + pertuzumab
endpoints: 16.8% pCR on dual HER2 blockade alone
takeaway: First trial establishing dual anti-HER2 blockade as the neoadjuvant standard. The chemo-free arm's 17% pCR was the first real signal that some HER2+ tumours might not need chemotherapy at all.

name: NIAGARA
population: Cisplatin-ELIGIBLE muscle-invasive bladder cancer — relatively earlier disease than KEYNOTE-905.
treatment: Durvalumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin → surgery → durvalumab vs gem/cis → observation
takeaway: Perioperative durvalumab added to gem/cis improves EFS and OS in cisplatin-eligible MIBC. Note the disconnect: big EFS/OS gain but only a modest pCR bump. No OS benefit seen in Asian, T2N0 or PD-L1-high subgroups.

name: NICHE-2
population: dMMR colon cancer, clinical stage I/II 12 pts, stage III 95 pts (89%). Lynch syndrome 32%.
treatment: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg × 2 doses + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg × 1 dose
endpoints: ✅ Major pathologic response 95%; pCR 68% (Lynch 79% vs non-Lynch 61%)
takeaway: Just three doses of neoadjuvant dual checkpoint blockade produced a 95% major pathologic response and zero recurrences in dMMR colon cancer — without delaying surgery.

name: NIVOPOST-OP
population: High-risk R0 locally advanced HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx/larynx) with ≥1 high-risk pathological feature: ENE 63%, positive margin 58%, ≥4 LN 13%, multiple PNI 56%. Oral cavity 58%; p16+ only 5%; stage pIVa–IVb 83%; CPS ≥20 in 36–43%, CPS negative 11–14%.
treatment: Nivolumab 240 mg ×1 → cisplatin-RT + nivolumab 360 mg q3w ×3 → nivolumab 480 mg q4w ×6 vs cisplatin-RT alone
takeaway: This is the first positive adjuvant ICI trial in high-risk locally advanced HNSCC, with the benefit driven by reduced locoregional recurrence alone. Caveats: OS is immature, DFS by BICR was not significant, and the row notes no FDA approval.

name: NO16968 (XELOXA)
population: Resected stage III colon cancer.
treatment: Adjuvant XELOX vs 5-FU/leucovorin × 6 months
takeaway: XELOX improves both DFS and OS in stage III colon cancer — the oral-fluoropyrimidine counterpart to MOSAIC, and it did reach OS significance.

name: NOAH
population: HER2+ locally advanced breast cancer (T3N1, T4, or N2/N3/supraclavicular) or inflammatory. HR+ 36%, age ≥50 in 57%, N1/N2 85%.
treatment: Perioperative trastuzumab + chemo ×10 → adjuvant trastuzumab ×7 (1 yr total) vs chemo alone
takeaway: First trial showing perioperative trastuzumab improves EFS and doubles pCR in locally advanced HER2+ disease. pCR predicts EFS benefit specifically in trastuzumab-treated patients.

name: NSABP B-18
population: Operable palpable breast cancer T1–3 N0–1, molecularly unselected. cN+ 26%, age <50 in 51%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant AC ×4 → surgery vs surgery → adjuvant AC ×4
endpoints: 9-yr OS 85% if pCR vs 73% if residual invasive disease
takeaway: Timing of chemotherapy doesn't matter for survival — neoadjuvant equals adjuvant. What it buys is more breast conservation, plus a prognostic readout: pCR predicts outcome. Laid the groundwork for FDA's 2014 pCR guidance.

name: NSABP B-27
population: Operable breast cancer T1c–T3 N0–N1, molecularly unselected. cN+ 30%, age <50 in 57%. Tamoxifen given to all ≥50 regardless of ER.
treatment: Neoadjuvant AC ×4 → surgery vs AC ×4 → docetaxel ×4 → surgery vs AC ×4 → surgery → adjuvant docetaxel ×4
endpoints: ✅ Preop docetaxel 26.1% vs AC alone 13.7%, P<0.001; postop docetaxel 13.7%
takeaway: Adding preoperative docetaxel doubled pCR and cut local recurrence — but never translated into DFS or OS benefit. The cleanest demonstration that pCR predicts individual outcome yet fails as a trial-level surrogate.

name: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831
population: HER2+ operable node-positive (both trials) or high-risk node-negative (N9831 only).
treatment: AC ×4 → taxane vs AC ×4 → taxane + trastuzumab → trastuzumab alone, 1 year total
takeaway: The landmark joint analysis that made adjuvant trastuzumab standard of care in HER2+ early breast cancer — a 40% reduction in recurrence and 37% in death.

name: OlympiA
population: gBRCA1/2, HER2− early breast cancer after surgery + neo/adjuvant chemotherapy; non-pCR or high-risk adjuvant. TNBC 82%, HR+/HER2− 18%; BRCA1 72% / BRCA2 27%. Median age 42; premenopausal ≈61%.
treatment: Adjuvant olaparib 300 mg PO BID × 1 year vs matching placebo, started after surgery, chemotherapy and RT (adjuvant endocrine therapy in HR+)
takeaway: One year of adjuvant olaparib improved IDFS, DDFS and OS in gBRCA1/2, HER2− high-risk early breast cancer, making it a new standard of care, with benefit across BRCA1/2 and HR status. Caveat: OS was significant only at the second interim analysis (P=0.009).

name: OPRA
population: Stage II/III rectal cancer; cT3 76–78%, N+ ~70%. Median distance from anal verge ~4.5 cm (low rectum, the group most wanting sphincter preservation).
treatment: Organ preservation: FOLFOX ×8 / CAPOX ×5 → LCRT vs LCRT → FOLFOX ×8 / CAPOX ×5 (both arms are TNT; compares sequence, not TNT vs non-TNT)
endpoints: ✅ cCR 40%, nCR 31% → 74% watch-and-wait (WW); ChT-CRT 72% WW (51% cCR) vs CRT-ChT 76% WW (58% cCR)
✅ TME-free survival 39% vs. 54%, P=.012; regrowth in WW 44% vs. 29%, P=.02 — both favour CRT-ChT
✅ Surgery after regrowth vs at initial restaging: 5-yr DFS 64% vs. 64% (P=.94)
takeaway: TNT lets about half of rectal cancer patients keep the rectum without sacrificing survival, and the sequence matters: CRT-ChT beats ChT-CRT on TME-free survival and regrowth. Surgery after regrowth costs nothing in DFS (64% vs 64%, R0 91% vs 90%), and 94% of regrowths occur within 2 years (99% within 3). Organ preservation is not cure: 13 of 144 patients (9%) with a sustained cCR still developed distant metastases, median 1.5 y from randomisation.

name: P024
population: Postmenopausal, HR+ (ER and/or PgR ≥10%), T2–4a-c N0–2 M0, ineligible for breast-conserving surgery.
treatment: Neoadjuvant letrozole 2.5 mg vs tamoxifen 20 mg daily × 4 months
takeaway: Neoadjuvant letrozole beats tamoxifen in postmenopausal women not eligible for breast conservation, converting more to lumpectomy. Effective even in HER2+ and marginally ER+ tumours.

name: PARADIGM (HNSCC)
population: Untreated stage III/IV non-metastatic SCC of oral cavity/oropharynx/hypopharynx/larynx — unresectable, low surgical curability, or organ-preservation candidates. WHO PS 0–1. Stage IV 86%, oropharynx 55%, N2 71%, T4 24%; median age 54. HPV status never tested.
treatment: Induction TPF ×3 → response-adapted chemoradiation vs cisplatin chemoradiation alone
takeaway: Induction TPF gave no OS or PFS benefit — both numerically favoured chemoradiation alone. Stopped early at 145 of 330 planned patients, and outcomes far exceeded the assumed 55% 3-yr OS, almost certainly unmeasured HPV+ disease. Response to induction was strongly prognostic (3-yr OS 92% vs 52%) but intensification did not rescue poor responders.

name: PEARLS / KEYNOTE-091
population: R0-resected NSCLC, stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA (AJCC 7th), ECOG 0–1. ~86% received adjuvant chemotherapy.
treatment: Pembrolizumab × 1 yr vs placebo; no crossover
takeaway: Adjuvant pembrolizumab improves DFS regardless of PD-L1 → FDA approved for stage IB–IIIA. Paradoxically, the PD-L1 ≥50% co-primary missed — the mirror image of IMpower010.

name: PICC
population: dMMR/MSI-H resectable locally advanced CRC (cT3–4 or any T N+). Colon 28, rectal 4, double primary 2. Stage II 4, stage III 30.
treatment: Toripalimab ×6 cycles q2w ± celecoxib
endpoints: ✅ 100% in both arms at median 14.9 mo
takeaway: Adding celecoxib to PD-1 blockade pushed pCR from 65% to 88% in dMMR locally advanced CRC — cheap, safe, and worth a larger trial.

name: PRODIGE 23
population: Locally advanced rectal cancer, cT3 (80%) or cT4, node-positive 90%.
treatment: TNT: FOLFIRINOX ×6 → long-course chemoRT → TME → FOLFOX ×6, vs chemoRT → TME → FOLFOX ×12
takeaway: Induction FOLFIRINOX before chemoradiation doubles pCR and improves DFS and metastasis-free survival, with a strong OS trend by 7 years.

name: PROSPECT
population: cT2N+ or cT3N0–1 rectal cancer in candidates for sphincter-sparing surgery; cT3 90%. Risk is lower than in other trials, since RT is being omitted.
treatment: Selective RT: neoadjuvant mFOLFOX6 ×6 vs standard LCRT
takeaway: In average-risk locally advanced rectal cancer eligible for sphincter-sparing surgery, neoadjuvant FOLFOX with selective chemoradiation was non-inferior to routine preoperative chemoradiation for DFS. About 90% avoided preoperative radiation with the FOLFOX strategy.

name: RAPIDO
population: HIGH-risk locally advanced rectal cancer: cT4 30%, cN2 65%, EMVI 30%, MRF+ 60%, enlarged lateral nodes 15%.
treatment: Short-course RT → CAPOX ×6 / FOLFOX ×9 → surgery (no adjuvant chemo) vs long-course chemoRT → surgery (+ adjuvant chemo in 41%)
takeaway: Short-course RT followed by consolidation chemo cuts distant metastases and doubles pCR in high-risk rectal cancer. The mechanism is compliance — patients actually complete chemotherapy before surgery, not after.

name: RxPONDER
population: HR+/HER2−, 1–3 positive nodes (N1), Oncotype RS ≤25. Median age 57.5; 33% premenopausal; RS 0–13 in 43%, RS 14–25 in 57%.
treatment: Endocrine therapy alone vs chemotherapy + endocrine therapy
endpoints: ❌ NOT MET — treatment × continuous RS interaction P=0.35
takeaway: In node-positive disease with RS ≤25, the Recurrence Score does NOT predict chemotherapy benefit — menopausal status does. Postmenopausal women can skip chemo; premenopausal women benefit. Whether that benefit is the chemotherapy itself or the ovarian suppression it causes remains unresolved.

name: SAMIT
population: Japanese, ECOG 0–1, advanced T4a/T4b gastric cancer after R0 + D2.
treatment: 2×2 design — paclitaxel→UFT vs paclitaxel→S-1 vs UFT alone vs S-1 alone
takeaway: S-1 beats UFT in advanced gastric cancer. Sequential paclitaxel adds nothing overall, though it may have a role in stage IIIB.

name: SOFT / TEXT
population: Pre/perimenopausal women with HR+ breast cancer. Higher-risk patients received chemotherapy and had to remain premenopausal afterwards.
treatment: SOFT: tamoxifen vs tamoxifen + OFS vs exemestane + OFS. TEXT: tamoxifen + OFS vs exemestane + OFS. 5 years
endpoints: ✅ Exemestane+OFS OS benefit confined to chemo-treated (high-risk) patients
takeaway: Premenopausal women benefit from ovarian function suppression for 5 years. In high-risk patients (those needing chemo, or under 35), an aromatase inhibitor with OFS beats tamoxifen with OFS.

name: STELLAR
population: Distal-middle rectal cancer, cT3–4 (15% cT4); N+ 85% (cN2 35%); MRF+ ~50%, EMVI ~50%.
treatment: SCRT → CAPOX ×4 → TME → CAPOX ×2 vs LCRT → TME → CAPOX ×6
takeaway: The row summarises TNT as improving DFS and OS: pCR and 3-yr OS were higher with SCRT-based TNT, while DFS met non-inferiority. Hematologic toxicity was increased.

name: TAILORx
population: Women 18–75, HR+/HER2−, NODE-NEGATIVE, meeting criteria for adjuvant chemo. In the randomised RS 11–25 cohort: median age 55, 36% premenopausal, median tumour 1.5 cm, 74% low clinical risk.
treatment: Oncotype DX 21-gene RS. RS 11–25 randomised to ET alone vs chemo + ET. RS ≤10 → ET alone; RS ≥26 → chemo + ET (non-randomised)
takeaway: In node-negative disease with RS 11–25, endocrine therapy alone is non-inferior — about 85% of these patients can skip chemotherapy. The exception: women ≤50 with RS 16–25, where chemo cut distant recurrence by 6.5% at 9 years.

name: Tislelizumab LANPC (NCT05211232)
population: High-risk locoregionally advanced NPC, stage III–IVa (AJCC 8th), excluding T3N0 and T3N1 with positive retropharyngeal nodes. Enrolled Jun 2022 – May 2023.
treatment: Tislelizumab + GP induction → CCRT → adjuvant tislelizumab ×8 vs placebo + same backbone
takeaway: Adding tislelizumab to GP induction deepens response without added toxicity, meeting the first of two co-primary endpoints. PFS is immature, so no survival claim yet — and this is an ASCO abstract only, so treat it as provisional. Do not confuse with RATIONALE-309 (metastatic NPC).

name: TRAIN-2
population: Stage II–III HER2+ breast cancer, treatment-naive. HR+ 59%, node+ 63%, grade 3 ~45%, median age ~48.
treatment: Anthracycline: FEC ×3 → paclitaxel/carboplatin ×6 + HP, vs anthracycline-free: paclitaxel/carboplatin ×9 + HP
endpoints: ✅ pCR vs no pCR 3-yr DFS HR 0.42 (0.23–0.78), P=0.006
takeaway: Anthracyclines add nothing to a carboplatin/taxane + dual HER2 backbone — equal pCR and EFS with far less toxicity. Helped establish anthracycline-free TCHP as the neoadjuvant standard.

name: TransNEOS
population: Postmenopausal women <75 y, ER+/HER2−, cN0, T1c–T2 (≥2 cm).
treatment: Neoadjuvant letrozole × 24–28 wk, stratified by Oncotype Recurrence Score (<18, 18–30, ≥31)
takeaway: Validates the 21-gene Recurrence Score as a predictor of response to neoadjuvant letrozole — low RS tumours are the ones that melt on endocrine therapy alone.

name: TRYPHAENA
population: HER2+ operable (T2–3 N0–1), locally advanced, or inflammatory breast cancer; primary tumour >2 cm. HR+ 37–64% across arms.
treatment: 3-arm cardiac safety study — A: FEC+HP ×3 → TPH ×3; B: FEC ×3 → TPH ×3; C: TCHP ×6 (anthracycline-free)
endpoints: ✅ Symptomatic LVSD: A 0%, B 2.7%, C 0%; all-grade 5.6% / 4.0% / 2.6%
takeaway: Dual HER2 blockade with or without anthracyclines carried low cardiotoxicity, and established anthracycline-free TCHP as a legitimate neoadjuvant option.

name: ABBV-400 (Temab-A)
population: Heavily pretreated CRC; c-Met unselected cohort (Part 5 enriched for MET-amplified).
treatment: Telisotuzumab adizutecan — c-Met–directed ADC with a topoisomerase-1 inhibitor payload
takeaway: Underwhelming activity in colorectal cancer — high disease control but a low response rate and short PFS.

name: ACOSOG Z9001
population: Primary KIT(CD117)+ GIST ≥3 cm after complete gross resection, registered ≤70 days post-op. Median age 58, median size 6.5 cm; 62% gastric / 32% small intestine; 91.5% R0.
treatment: Adjuvant imatinib 400 mg/d × 1 year vs placebo
endpoints: ✅ Median NR — HR 0.60 (0.43–0.75), P<0.001; separation sustained at 74-mo follow-up
takeaway: One year of adjuvant imatinib gives a durable RFS benefit but no OS benefit. Size, location and mitotic rate — not genotype — define GIST's natural history, and imatinib benefit concentrates in KIT exon 11 deletions.

name: ADRIATIC
population: Limited-stage small cell lung cancer with no progression after definitive concurrent chemoradiation.
treatment: Consolidation durvalumab vs placebo
takeaway: Consolidation durvalumab after definitive chemoradiation in limited-stage SCLC improves both OS and PFS — a 22-month median OS gain. More discontinuation for adverse events.

name: AK105-304 (penpulimab)
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC. Global study across 46 sites with an ethnically diverse population — unlike the endemic East-Asian cohorts of the other first-line trials. 46% crossover.
treatment: Penpulimab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + GP, induction then maintenance
takeaway: The generalisability trial — basis of the first FDA approval of a PD-1 inhibitor in this setting (April 2025). Numerically the lowest PFS hazard ratio of its class, though crossover was permitted so cross-trial comparison isn't justified. Carboplatin was allowed, making it the most flexible regimen for cisplatin-unfit patients.

name: ALEX
population: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC (details not yet captured in your database).
treatment: Alectinib vs crizotinib
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder entry — the trial that established alectinib over crizotinib in first-line ALK+ NSCLC. Worth filling in.

name: ASCENT
population: Metastatic TNBC with ≥2 prior chemotherapies. 100% prior taxane, 82% prior anthracycline, 27% prior ICI. Notably, 30% were NOT triple-negative at initial diagnosis.
treatment: Sacituzumab govitecan vs physician's-choice single-agent chemo (eribulin 54%, vinorelbine 20%, capecitabine 13%, gemcitabine 12%). No crossover
takeaway: Sacituzumab govitecan decisively beats single-agent chemo in late-line metastatic TNBC on OS, PFS and ORR. Cost is myelosuppression and diarrhoea. The 30% who weren't TNBC at diagnosis is a reminder that re-biopsy at recurrence matters.

name: ASCENT-03
population: Treatment-naive TNBC, ineligible for ICI. Disease-free interval 6–12 mo in 21% and >12 mo in 48%; de novo 31%; brain metastases 5%.
treatment: Sacituzumab govitecan (SG) vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (T, nab-T or GC); crossover to SG 80%
takeaway: First-line SG beat chemotherapy in PD-L1-negative TNBC, addressing a real gap since CPS <10 accounts for about 60% of metastatic TNBC. Caveats: 6 treatment-related deaths, all from infection, so consider primary G-CSF prophylaxis; OS is immature and confounded by crossover.

name: ASCENT-04
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS ≥10. De novo 34%, DFI 6–12 mo 18%, >12 mo 48%, brain mets 3–4%.
treatment: Sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab vs chemo + pembrolizumab
takeaway: Swapping chemo for sacituzumab govitecan alongside pembrolizumab improves PFS in first-line PD-L1-positive metastatic TNBC, with a much lower discontinuation rate (12% vs 31%).

name: ASPECCT
population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type colorectal cancer progressing after oxaliplatin, irinotecan and fluoropyrimidine. ECOG 0–2.
treatment: Panitumumab vs cetuximab
takeaway: Panitumumab is non-inferior to cetuximab in chemotherapy-refractory, KRAS exon 2 wild-type metastatic CRC.

name: ASPECT
population: Not captured in your database.
treatment: Anti-VEGF (details not entered)
takeaway: Cetuximab and panitumumab have equivalent efficacy. (Row is sparse — may be a duplicate of ASPECCT worth merging or filling in.)

name: ATTRACTION-3
population: ESCC only; one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy. Asian 96%; prior surgery 49%, prior RT 70%; tumour-cell PD-L1 ≥1% in 48%.
treatment: Nivolumab 240 mg Q2W vs taxane (open-label)
endpoints: ❌ 1.7 vs 3.4 mo — HR 1.08 (0.87–1.34); but 12-mo PFS 12% vs 7% (late crossing curves)
takeaway: Nivolumab improved OS over taxane in 2L ESCC despite worse PFS and ORR, and is the standard of care in this setting. Benefit was regardless of PD-L1, and the PFS-negative but OS-positive pattern reflects a delayed immunotherapy effect.

name: AVEX
population: ELDERLY (≥70 years) mCRC, ECOG 0–2 — patients not considered fit for doublet chemotherapy.
treatment: Bevacizumab + capecitabine vs capecitabine alone
takeaway: For elderly patients unfit for doublets, bevacizumab + capecitabine nearly doubles PFS — a practical first-line option.

name: AVF2107g (Hurwitz)
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG 0–1 (adjuvant therapy allowed if ≥1 yr prior).
treatment: Bevacizumab + IFL (irinotecan/5-FU/LV) vs IFL alone
takeaway: The first trial showing bevacizumab improves survival in metastatic colorectal cancer — a 4.7-month OS gain that launched anti-angiogenic therapy in solid tumours.

name: BEACON
population: BRAF V600E-mutant CRC. Right-sided primary 50–60%; 35% had 2 prior regimens.
treatment: Encorafenib + binimetinib + cetuximab vs encorafenib + cetuximab (EC) vs E-ChT
takeaway: Encorafenib + cetuximab with or without binimetinib gave an OS benefit in ≥2L BRAF V600E-mutant CRC. The doublet (EC) appears to be enough, since its results are close to the triplet's.

name: Beamion Lung-01
population: HER2-mutant NSCLC (details not yet captured).
treatment: Zongertinib — HER2-selective TKI
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder entry for the zongertinib trial in HER2-mutant NSCLC. Worth filling in.

name: BFR14
population: Advanced CD117+ GIST, imatinib-naive at entry, in CR/PR/SD after 1 year of imatinib 400 mg/d. 58 randomised of 182 enrolled. Median age 62, ECOG 0–1 in 88%, 82% metastatic.
treatment: Imatinib interruption vs continuous imatinib 400 mg/d, randomised after 1 year of disease control
endpoints: ⚠️ 6.1 vs 18.0 mo, P<0.0001 — strongly favours continuation
takeaway: Stopping imatinib in responding advanced GIST causes rapid progression — even in radiologic CR. Reintroduction restores control in 92% with no OS or resistance penalty, but interruption still cannot be recommended.

name: BOLERO-2
population: Postmenopausal women with ER+/HER2− advanced or metastatic breast cancer refractory to a non-steroidal AI. 84% had prior endocrine sensitivity, 68% prior chemotherapy, ~54% were third line or later.
treatment: Everolimus + exemestane vs placebo + exemestane
endpoints: ⚠️ 31.0 vs 26.6 mo — HR 0.89 (0.73–1.10), P=0.1426, NS; post-progression survival 20.8 vs 19.3 mo
takeaway: This was the first mTOR inhibitor plus endocrine therapy to show a PFS benefit after NSAI failure, establishing PI3K/AKT/mTOR as a validated target in endocrine resistance. The PFS gain did not translate into a significant OS difference.

name: BOND
population: Irinotecan-refractory mCRC, EGFR-inhibitor naive.
treatment: Cetuximab + irinotecan vs cetuximab alone
takeaway: Continuing irinotecan alongside cetuximab doubles response rate even in irinotecan-refractory disease — cetuximab appears to reverse irinotecan resistance.

name: BREAKWATER
population: Previously untreated BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC. dMMR excluded.
treatment: Encorafenib + cetuximab + FOLFOX vs standard-of-care chemotherapy
takeaway: Moves BRAF-targeted therapy to first line and doubles median OS from 15 to 30 months — transformative for a subgroup that historically had the worst prognosis in colorectal cancer.

name: BYLieve
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with PIK3CA mutation, progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (cohort A). ≤2 prior advanced lines, ≤1 prior chemo.
treatment: Alpelisib + fulvestrant (single-arm, no control)
takeaway: Confirms alpelisib + fulvestrant retains activity specifically after CDK4/6 inhibitor failure — the population SOLAR-1 didn't cover.

name: CAIRO2
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG ≤1, KRAS status unselected.
treatment: Cetuximab + bevacizumab + CAPOX vs bevacizumab + CAPOX
takeaway: Combining anti-EGFR with anti-VEGF made outcomes worse, not better. Dual biologic blockade is not additive in colorectal cancer — don't combine them.

name: CAIRO3
population: mCRC in CR/PR/SD after 6 cycles of induction bevacizumab-CAPOX. CR/PR in 65%.
treatment: Maintenance bevacizumab + capecitabine vs observation
takeaway: Maintenance bev + capecitabine after induction delays second progression — the benefit survives re-induction at progression, which is what PFS2 was designed to test.

name: CAIRO5
population: mCRC with initially unresectable liver-only metastases, ECOG 0–1, stratified by right primary tumour or RAS/BRAF mutation.
treatment: Group A/B (right-sided or RAS/RAF-mut): bev-doublet vs bev-triplet (FOLFOXIRI). Group C/D (left-sided RAS/RAF-wt): bev-doublet vs panitumumab-doublet
takeaway: For right-sided or RAS/RAF-mutant liver-limited disease, a bevacizumab triplet improves PFS and conversion to resectability. For left-sided RAS/RAF wild-type, adding panitumumab to a doublet raises response rate but not PFS.

name: CALGB 150105 / SWOG S0033 (genotype)
population: Advanced CD117+ GIST on first-line imatinib; 428 of 746 successfully genotyped (95.7% success). Genotypes: KIT exon 11 71.3%, KIT exon 9 8.2%, wild-type 17%. Median follow-up 4.5 yr.
treatment: Prospective genotype–outcome correlative study within imatinib 400 mg/d vs 800 mg/d
endpoints: ✅ 24.7 vs 16.7 vs 12.8 mo — exon 9 HR 2.07, WT HR 1.85 vs exon 11
✅ 60.0 vs 38.4 vs 49.0 mo; dose had no effect on OS in any genotype
takeaway: KIT exon 11 is the genotype that responds best to imatinib on every measure. Exon 9 tumours respond far better to 800 mg — but the higher dose changed neither time to progression nor overall survival in any genotype.

name: CALGB / SWOG 80405
population: KRAS wild-type mCRC, ECOG ≤1, previously untreated.
treatment: Cetuximab vs bevacizumab, each added to FOLFIRI or mFOLFOX6 (a cetuximab+bevacizumab arm was dropped early)
takeaway: Cetuximab and bevacizumab are interchangeable as the first-line biologic in KRAS wild-type mCRC — median OS ~29 months either way. What determines outcome is the whole treatment sequence, not the first biologic. (Sidedness analyses later refined this.)

name: CAPItello-291
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer relapsing/progressing during or after an AI. ~70% had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. Enrolled regardless of PAM-pathway alteration; diabetics with HbA1c <8.0% allowed.
treatment: Capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Capivasertib doubles PFS after AI failure, with the benefit concentrated in PAM-pathway-altered tumours. No OS benefit in either population.

name: CAPTAIN-1st
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC, all Asian (China-only). Liver mets ~50%, baseline EBV DNA positive ~70%, 64% with prior chemoradiation.
treatment: Camrelizumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + GP, induction then maintenance. No crossover
takeaway: The only R/M NPC trial with 5-year follow-up and the current long-term benchmark. Caveat: OS was not multiplicity-controlled and the P value is marginal. Directly actionable finding — rapid plasma EBV DNA clearance within 3 cycles separated 5-yr OS of 46.8% from 7.5%, and 97% of 5-year survivors were EBV-negative at baseline or cleared early.

name: CARES-310
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; ~80% Asian; VP4 excluded.
treatment: Camrelizumab + rivoceranib (n=272) vs sorafenib (n=271)
endpoints: ✅ ORR 25 vs 6; DCR 80 vs 54; DoR 14.8 vs 9.2 mo
takeaway: Camrelizumab + rivoceranib beat sorafenib on OS, PFS and ORR in first-line unresectable HCC. Caveats: toxicity was high (≥Gr3 AE 80%) and the population was ~80% Asian.

name: CASPIAN
population: Treatment-naive extensive-stage SCLC, PS 0–1. Stable CNS metastases allowed.
treatment: Durvalumab + etoposide/platinum ×4 → durvalumab maintenance vs EP ×6 (a durva + tremelimumab + EP arm was also studied)
takeaway: Established chemo-immunotherapy as the first-line standard in extensive-stage SCLC. Note the PFS curves barely separate — as so often with ICI, the benefit is in the tail.

name: CELESTIAL
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C, progressing on sorafenib. Only 1 patient was truly second line.
treatment: Cabozantinib (n=470) vs placebo (n=237)
takeaway: Cabozantinib improved both OS and PFS over placebo in HCC after sorafenib. Almost all patients were effectively third line, so this is mainly evidence for later-line use.

name: CLEOPATRA
population: Treatment-naive HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. Prior (neo)adjuvant chemo allowed if ≥12-month interval. 88% visceral disease.
treatment: Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel vs placebo + trastuzumab + docetaxel
takeaway: Dual HER2 blockade with docetaxel (THP) became the first-line standard for HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, with a 16-month median OS gain and a genuine long-term plateau.

name: CheckMate-040
population: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A or B7.
treatment: Nivolumab (single-arm; dose-escalation and expansion)
takeaway: Nivolumab produced a 20% ORR with durable responses in advanced HCC, in sorafenib-naive or -treated patients including Child-Pugh B7. This led to FDA accelerated approval in 2017, later withdrawn after CM-459.

name: CheckMate-275
population: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma after ≥1 line of platinum chemotherapy.
treatment: Nivolumab monotherapy (single-arm)
takeaway: Single-agent nivolumab has modest activity in platinum-refractory urothelial carcinoma, roughly doubling median OS in PD-L1-positive vs negative patients.

name: CheckMate-459
population: Child-Pugh A; macrovascular invasion 30%.
treatment: Nivolumab (n=371) vs sorafenib (n=372)
takeaway: Nivolumab did not significantly beat sorafenib for OS (not significant) and PFS was negative in first-line unresectable HCC. It did give a higher ORR (15% vs 7%) and fewer grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs, and the FDA 2L accelerated approval was withdrawn.

name: CheckMate-648
population: Almost all ESCC; 70% Asian; tumour-cell PD-L1 ≥1% in 49%.
treatment: Nivolumab + PF (chemo) vs nivolumab + ipilimumab vs chemo (open-label, 1:1:1, N=970)
endpoints: ⚠️ Nivo-ChT 5.8 vs ChT 5.6 mo — HR 0.81 (98.5% CI 0.64–1.04), P=0.04 (boundary 0.015 not met); ❌ Nivo-ipi 2.9 vs 5.6 — HR 1.26 (95% CI 1.04–1.52), not formally tested
✅ PD-L1 ≥1%: 53 vs 35 vs 20 (Nivo-ChT / Nivo-ipi / ChT); overall 47 vs 28 vs 27
takeaway: Both nivolumab + chemo and nivolumab + ipilimumab improved OS over chemo in ITT and in the PD-L1 ≥1% population, and both are 1L ESCC standards of care. Nivo-ipi PFS was negative in ITT, and the benefit is driven by tumour-cell PD-L1 ≥1% (HR ~1 if PD-L1 <1%). Nivo-ipi also had 30% early progression.

name: CheckMate-8HW
population: dMMR/MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer. 60% right-sided, 25% BRAF-mutant, 20% RAS-mutant.
treatment: Nivolumab + ipilimumab vs nivolumab alone vs chemotherapy
takeaway: Dual checkpoint blockade beats nivolumab alone in dMMR mCRC, mainly by preventing early progression. Nivolumab monotherapy may still suffice in right-sided or RAS/BRAF-mutant disease.

name: CheckMate-901
population: Cisplatin-eligible patients only. UTUC 23%; Asian 25%.
treatment: Nivolumab + GP vs GP
takeaway: Nivolumab + GP improved both PFS and OS in cisplatin-eligible 1L urothelial carcinoma. Only cisplatin-eligible patients were enrolled because IMvigor130 and KN-361 suggested cisplatin gives better survival than carboplatin.

name: CheckMate-9DW
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; ~40% Asian; VP4 excluded.
treatment: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (n=335) vs lenvatinib (85%) / sorafenib (n=333)
takeaway: Nivolumab + ipilimumab beat lenvatinib/sorafenib on OS and ORR (36%, DoR 30.4 mo) in first-line unresectable HCC, but PFS was negative. Caveats: early KM curve crossover, and ≥Gr3 irAEs ~30% (hepatitis), mostly within the first 6 months.

name: CodeBreaK 300
population: Chemorefractory KRAS G12C-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer.
treatment: Sotorasib 960 mg or 240 mg + panitumumab vs trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib
takeaway: KRAS G12C inhibition finally works in colorectal cancer when paired with EGFR blockade — the same lesson BEACON taught for BRAF. Full dose is clearly better.

name: CodeBreaK 301
population: Treatment-naive KRAS G12C-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer.
treatment: Sotorasib + panitumumab + FOLFIRI vs bevacizumab-FOLFIRI
endpoints: ⏳ Ongoing — no phase III results yet
ORR 57.5%, DCR 92.5%, PFS 8.2 mo, OS 17.9 mo
takeaway: Moving the sotorasib-panitumumab combination to first line. The phase I signal (ORR 58%) is strong; the phase III will decide.

name: CONFIRM
population: Postmenopausal HR+ advanced breast cancer progressing after prior endocrine therapy.
treatment: Fulvestrant 500 mg (q2w loading then monthly) vs 250 mg monthly
takeaway: Simple dose optimisation: 500 mg fulvestrant beats 250 mg on both PFS and OS with no added toxicity. Established the 500 mg dose used in every subsequent combination trial.

name: CORRECT
population: Heavily pretreated mCRC — about half had ≥4 prior regimens. ECOG 0 in 52–57%.
treatment: Regorafenib vs placebo
endpoints: ✅ 6.4 vs 5.0 mo — HR 0.77 (0.64–0.94), P=0.005 — absolute gain only 1.4 mo
takeaway: The first non-biomarker-selected third-line option in mCRC. Statistically positive but clinically modest — a 1.4-month median OS gain with real toxicity, which is why patient selection matters.

name: COSMIC-312
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C. Asian 30%, VP4 20%.
treatment: Atezolizumab + cabozantinib (n=432) vs sorafenib (n=217)
takeaway: Atezolizumab plus cabozantinib improved PFS but not OS against sorafenib in first-line unresectable HCC, and it was not approved. Grade 5 AEs occurred in 12%.

name: CROWN
population: Previously untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC, ECOG 0–2. Asymptomatic treated or untreated CNS metastases allowed.
treatment: Lorlatinib vs crizotinib
takeaway: Median PFS still not reached at 5 years, with 60% of patients progression-free — the longest reported PFS of any single-agent targeted therapy in any metastatic solid tumour. Intracranial control is near-absolute (94% risk reduction).

name: CRYSTAL
population: Previously untreated EGFR-expressing mCRC, ECOG ≤2, KRAS status unselected at enrolment (analysed retrospectively).
treatment: Cetuximab + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI
takeaway: Improved PFS but not OS overall — and the retrospective KRAS analysis showed benefit confined to wild-type tumours. One of the trials that made RAS testing mandatory before anti-EGFR therapy.

name: dd-MVAC (Sternberg)
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-eligible.
treatment: Dose-dense MVAC q2w (with G-CSF) vs classic MVAC q4w
takeaway: Compressing MVAC to every 2 weeks with growth factor support improves response and survival while reducing toxicity. Still more toxic than gem/cis, which is why GC dominates practice.

name: DeFi
population: Progressing desmoid tumours. Median age 34, 64% female, 77% previously treated (median 2 lines), 24% prior sorafenib. 41% multifocal, 75% extra-abdominal.
treatment: Nirogacestat 150 mg BID vs placebo — an oral γ-secretase (Notch) inhibitor
endpoints: ✅ 41% vs 8%, P<0.001; median time to response 5.6 mo
✅ NE vs 15.1 mo — HR 0.29 (0.15–0.55), P<0.001; consistent across all subgroups
✅ All 7 improved — pain, symptoms, physical and role function, QoL
takeaway: First FDA-approved therapy for desmoid tumours, with a 71% reduction in progression risk and benefit across every patient-reported outcome. Prior sorafenib did not blunt the effect. Watch GI, skin and ovarian toxicity.

name: DeLLphi-304
population: SCLC after 1L chemotherapy; no DLL3 requirement. Stable brain mets 45%; prior ICI 71%; chemo-free interval <90 d ~45%.
treatment: Tarlatamab vs chemotherapy (topotecan 73%, lubinectedin 18%, amrubicin 9%)
takeaway: Tarlatamab improved PFS and OS over chemotherapy in 2L SCLC. Cytokine release syndrome was notable (56%, mostly grade 1–2) and ICANS infrequent (6%).

name: DeLLphi-305
population: Extensive-stage SCLC entering maintenance after first-line chemo-immunotherapy.
treatment: Maintenance tarlatamab + durvalumab vs durvalumab alone
endpoints: 1-yr OS 80% per phase I DeLLphi-303 (vs ~60% 9-mo OS in IMpower133)
takeaway: Moving tarlatamab into first-line maintenance. Early single-arm signal looks strong but is not a randomised comparison.

name: DESTINY PanTumor-02
cancer: Pan-tumour (UC, endometrial, cervical, ovary, BTC, other)
population: Advanced solid tumours after ≥1 prior line, HER2 2+ or 3+ by gastric cancer criteria.
treatment: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-Dxd), single-arm
takeaway: Trastuzumab deruxtecan showed activity across HER2-expressing solid tumours, with the most benefit in centrally confirmed HER2 3+ disease.

name: DESTINY-Breast03
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer; prior trastuzumab + taxane required. N=524 (T-DXd n=261, T-DM1 n=263); ~62% prior pertuzumab; ~70% visceral disease; ~16% baseline CNS mets.
treatment: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) vs T-DM1
takeaway: T-DXd beat T-DM1 in second-line HER2+ metastatic breast cancer on PFS (28.8 vs 6.8, HR 0.28) and OS (52.6 vs 42.7, HR 0.73). The row notes this is the longest reported OS in this setting and that T-DXd is the second-line standard.

name: DESTINY-Breast09
population: Treatment-naive HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. Prior (neo)adjuvant chemo allowed if ≥12-mo interval. 73.4% visceral disease, 6.5% CNS mets, 54% HR+.
treatment: T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP (taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab)
takeaway: Directly challenges the CLEOPATRA-THP standard, extending first-line PFS past 40 months. Watch for interstitial lung disease — the recurring cost of T-DXd.

name: DESTINY-Breast12
population: HER2+ advanced breast cancer with ≥1 prior anti-HER2 regimen, ≤2 prior metastatic regimens, tucatinib-naive. Two cohorts: brain metastases (n=263, stable or ACTIVE) and no brain metastases (n=241).
treatment: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3w (single-arm)
endpoints: NR; 12-mo OS ~90% in both cohorts, immature
takeaway: T-DXd works in the brain — 72% intracranial response — and works whether the brain metastases are stable or active. Removes the old reason to reach for tucatinib first.

name: DESTINY-CRC01
population: HER2-expressing, RAS wild-type mCRC. Prior anti-HER2 therapy allowed. Median 4 prior lines.
treatment: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (single-arm, by HER2 IHC cohort)
takeaway: Striking activity in HER2 IHC 3+ colorectal cancer and literally zero responses below that — including IHC 2+/FISH+. Unlike breast cancer, there is no HER2-low story in CRC. DESTINY-CRC02 settled 5.4 mg/kg as the dose.

name: EMBRACA
population: Germline BRCA1/2-mutant, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with ≤3 prior chemotherapy lines. Prior taxane and anthracycline required; prior platinum for metastatic disease allowed.
treatment: Talazoparib vs physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy
takeaway: Talazoparib more than doubles response rate and improves PFS in germline BRCA-mutant metastatic breast cancer, but no OS benefit — likely diluted by heavy crossover and later-line enrolment compared with OlympiAD.

name: EMERALD
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on prior endocrine therapy; ≤1 prior chemo. ALL required prior CDK4/6 inhibitor plus fulvestrant or AI. 47.8% ESR1-mutant; visceral mets ~68–71%.
treatment: Elacestrant (oral SERD) vs standard-of-care endocrine therapy
takeaway: First oral SERD to show PFS benefit after CDK4/6 inhibitor failure, with the effect concentrated in ESR1-mutant disease (45% vs 30% risk reduction). Be honest about scale: the ITT median PFS gain is under a month.

name: EMILIA
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer with prior trastuzumab and taxane. No prior T-DM1, lapatinib or capecitabine.
treatment: T-DM1 vs lapatinib + capecitabine
endpoints: ✅ 30.9 vs 25.1 mo — HR 0.68 (0.55–0.85), P<0.001 (27% crossover by final analysis)
takeaway: The first antibody-drug conjugate to beat chemotherapy on both PFS and OS, with less toxicity. Made T-DM1 the second-line standard — a position it held until DESTINY-Breast03.

name: EORTC 62024
population: Localised intermediate-/high-risk GIST after R0–R1 resection. Median age 59, 86% PS 0, 55% gastric, 11% tumour rupture. 112 centres, 12 countries.
treatment: Adjuvant imatinib 400 mg/d × 2 years vs observation
takeaway: Two years of adjuvant imatinib improved RFS but missed its primary endpoint and showed no OS benefit — and by 10 years the RFS curves converge. Adjuvant imatinib delays relapse rather than curing it.

name: EV-301
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma progressing after BOTH platinum chemotherapy AND a checkpoint inhibitor. ECOG 0–1.
treatment: Enfortumab vedotin vs physician's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: Enfortumab vedotin delivers a clear OS benefit in the hardest urothelial population — progressed on both platinum and ICI. Watch skin toxicity, hyperglycaemia and peripheral neuropathy.

name: EV-302
population: ECOG 0–2, eGFR ≥30. UTUC 30%; Asian 23%; cisplatin-eligible 54%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + enfortumab vedotin vs GP/GC
takeaway: Pembrolizumab + enfortumab vedotin beat platinum-gemcitabine on both PFS and OS in 1L urothelial carcinoma, and is the current standard of care.

name: FALCON
population: Postmenopausal HR+ advanced breast cancer, ENDOCRINE-THERAPY NAIVE.
treatment: Fulvestrant 500 mg vs anastrozole
endpoints: ⚠️ Non-visceral 22.3 vs 13.8 mo; ❌ visceral 13.8 vs 15.9 mo
takeaway: Fulvestrant beats anastrozole in endocrine-naive disease — but the entire benefit comes from non-visceral disease, where PFS is 22 vs 14 months. In visceral disease it was numerically worse.

name: FIRE-3
population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC, ECOG ≤2, previously untreated (adjuvant allowed if ≥6 months prior).
treatment: Cetuximab vs bevacizumab, both with FOLFIRI
endpoints: ❌ 62.0% vs 58.0% — OR 1.18, P=0.18, primary endpoint missed
takeaway: The trial that argued for anti-EGFR first in RAS wild-type mCRC — a 7.5-month OS gain in RAS wild-type despite identical response rate and PFS. Note the tension with CALGB 80405, which found no difference; sidedness later reconciled them.

name: FLAURA
population: Treatment-naive EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC — Ex19del 60%, L858R 40%. Stable brain mets 40%. Crossover allowed.
treatment: Osimertinib vs gefitinib or erlotinib
takeaway: Established first-line osimertinib as standard of care in EGFR-mutant NSCLC — near-doubled PFS and an OS benefit that survived crossover.

name: FLAURA2
population: Treatment-naive EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC — Ex19del 60%, L858R 40%. Stable brain mets 40% (brain MRI at baseline only). Crossover allowed.
treatment: Osimertinib + platinum/pemetrexed vs osimertinib alone
takeaway: Adding chemotherapy to osimertinib extends both PFS and OS — but at a real toxicity cost, so reserve it for high-risk patients: CNS or liver metastases, TP53 co-mutation, or persistent ctDNA.

name: FRESCO-2
population: Refractory mCRC — median 4 prior regimens, all had received TAS-102 and/or regorafenib. ECOG 0 in ~33%.
treatment: Fruquintinib vs placebo
takeaway: A genuine OS benefit after TAS-102 and regorafenib have already failed — extends the refractory treatment sequence by one more line.

name: Gem-carboplatin (EORTC 30986)
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-INELIGIBLE.
treatment: Gemcitabine + carboplatin vs methotrexate/carboplatin/vinblastine (M-CAVI)
takeaway: Established gem/carbo as the chemotherapy backbone for cisplatin-ineligible patients — better tolerated than M-CAVI with similar survival. Now largely superseded by EV-pembrolizumab.

name: Gem-cis
population: Cisplatin-eligible patients.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin vs MVAC (n=405, 1:1)
takeaway: Gemcitabine plus cisplatin is non-inferior to MVAC in cisplatin-eligible patients, with significantly less toxicity.

name: GERCOR (Tournigand)
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG ≤2 (adjuvant allowed if ≥6 months prior).
treatment: FOLFIRI → FOLFOX vs FOLFOX → FOLFIRI (sequence comparison)
endpoints: PFS1 8.5 vs 8.0 mo; PFS2 4.2 vs 2.5 mo; time to 2nd progression 14.2 vs 10.9 mo, P=0.64
takeaway: The order doesn't matter — what matters is that patients receive all three active agents (oxaliplatin, irinotecan, fluorouracil) across their treatment course. FOLFOX does work better than FOLFIRI in second line.

name: HER2CLIMB
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1. ECOG 0–1. Uniquely, ACTIVE and untreated brain metastases were allowed (~47%).
treatment: Tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine vs placebo + trastuzumab + capecitabine
endpoints: ✅ PFS HR 0.48, P<0.001 — benefit fully maintained
takeaway: The first regimen designed around brain metastases, and the first HER2 trial to enrol patients with active untreated CNS disease. Improves OS in heavily pretreated disease with CNS benefit intact.

name: HERACLES-A
population: KRAS wild-type, HER2-amplified refractory mCRC. Prior anti-HER2 therapy excluded.
treatment: Trastuzumab + lapatinib (single-arm)
takeaway: First proof that dual HER2 blockade is active in HER2-amplified colorectal cancer — opened HER2 as a therapeutic target in a disease where it affects only ~3% of patients.

name: HIMALAYA
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Asian 40%; VP4 excluded.
treatment: Durvalumab + tremelimumab (n=393) vs sorafenib (n=389)
endpoints: ❌ STRIDE vs sorafenib 3.78 vs 4.07 — HR 0.90 (0.77–1.05); durvalumab vs sorafenib 3.65 vs 4.07 — HR 1.02 (0.88–1.19)
✅ STRIDE vs durvalumab vs sorafenib 20.1% vs 17% vs 5.1%
takeaway: STRIDE improved OS over sorafenib in 1L unresectable HCC and became standard of care, though PFS was not improved. Durvalumab monotherapy was non-inferior for OS, and there was a durable tail (5-yr OS ~15%) with fewer grade ≥3 TRAEs than sorafenib.

name: IMbrave 150
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; VP4 14%; esophageal varices not fully excluded.
treatment: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg (n=336) vs sorafenib (n=165)
takeaway: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab beat sorafenib on OS, PFS and ORR in first-line unresectable HCC and became standard of care. ≥Gr3 adverse events were similar to sorafenib, but EGD is required before bevacizumab because of varices.

name: IMforte
population: Treatment-naive extensive-stage SCLC with no progression after 4 cycles of IMpower133-style induction. ECOG 0–1. CNS metastases excluded.
treatment: Maintenance lurbinectedin + atezolizumab vs atezolizumab alone
takeaway: Adding lurbinectedin to maintenance atezolizumab improves OS in extensive-stage SCLC — the first real advance in maintenance since IMpower133. More haematologic toxicity; G-CSF is mandatory.

name: IMpower150
population: Chemo-naive non-squamous NSCLC. 13% had progressed on a prior TKI (EGFR/ALK) — most reported data is the wild-type population.
treatment: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab + carboplatin/paclitaxel (ABCP) vs bevacizumab + chemo vs atezolizumab + chemo
endpoints: ✅ Wild-type 8.3 vs 6.8 mo — HR 0.62 (0.52–0.74), P<0.001; EGFR/ALK-mutant 9.7 vs 6.1 mo
takeaway: The four-drug ABCP regimen improves OS in non-squamous NSCLC, and notably retains activity in the EGFR/ALK-mutant subgroup after TKI failure — where ICI usually fails.

name: IMpower133
population: Treatment-naive extensive-stage SCLC. Stable CNS metastases allowed.
treatment: Atezolizumab + etoposide/carboplatin → atezolizumab maintenance vs placebo + EC
takeaway: The first trial in 20 years to improve survival in extensive-stage SCLC. Modest in absolute terms (2 months) but it defined the chemo-immunotherapy backbone.

name: INAVO-120
population: PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2− locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, relapsing DURING or ≤12 months after adjuvant endocrine therapy — deliberately the highest-risk, endocrine-resistant group. De novo metastatic excluded. HbA1c <6.0% required. 93% ctDNA PIK3CA-positive.
treatment: Inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + palbociclib + fulvestrant
endpoints: ✅ NR vs 31.1 mo — HR 0.64 (0.43–0.97); OS benefit confirmed at ASCO 2025
takeaway: A triplet that doubles PFS and now shows an OS benefit in the most endocrine-resistant PIK3CA-mutant population. Inavolisib's mutant selectivity means better tolerability than alpelisib.

name: JAVELIN Bladder 100
population: Disease control after GP/GC. UTUC 30%; Asian 23%; cisplatin-eligible 55%.
treatment: Maintenance avelumab vs best supportive care
takeaway: Maintenance avelumab after disease control on GP/GC improved PFS and OS over best supportive care. There was no OS benefit in PD-L1-negative patients.

name: JUPITER-02
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC, predominantly in China. Liver mets ~40%, baseline EBV-positive ~60%, 45% prior chemoradiation.
treatment: Toripalimab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + GP, induction then maintenance. No crossover
takeaway: Largest first-line R/M NPC trial and the first to show a clear OS benefit. Cleanest demonstration that adding PD-1 blockade to GP doesn't raise total grade ≥3 toxicity (chemo dominates that) but roughly doubles immune-related AEs. No crossover and only ~13% control-arm ICI use makes the OS signal genuinely interpretable.

name: KANDLELIT-012
population: Not yet entered in your database.
treatment: Not entered
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — nothing captured yet
takeaway: Empty placeholder row in your Notion DB — worth filling in or removing.

name: KCSG-LU15-09
population: UNCOMMON EGFR mutations — G719X 53%, L861Q 25%, S768I 22%. No prior EGFR-TKI. 61% first-line, 25% baseline CNS metastases.
treatment: Osimertinib 80 mg daily (single-arm)
takeaway: First prospective evidence for osimertinib in uncommon EGFR mutations. L861Q is the standout — 78% response and 15-month PFS, outperforming historical afatinib data.

name: KEYNOTE-122
population: Platinum-pretreated, EBV-positive recurrent/metastatic NPC. Global trial; 86.7% were second line or later, 50% liver mets, 88% prior radiotherapy. Post-protocol crossover 60%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs investigator's-choice chemo (capecitabine 33%, gemcitabine 40%, docetaxel 25%)
takeaway: Negative trial, and the standing evidence that benefit in R/M NPC requires BOTH a chemotherapy backbone AND the first-line setting. The one clear win is toxicity — a four-fold reduction in severe AEs, which may still matter for a heavily pretreated patient prioritising quality of life.

name: KEYNOTE-016
population: Not entered in your database.
treatment: Not entered
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — nothing captured yet
takeaway: Empty placeholder — this is the landmark Le et al. trial that first showed dMMR predicts PD-1 response across tumour types. Worth filling in.

name: KEYNOTE-024
population: Treatment-naive advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, any histology. EGFR/ALK excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs platinum chemotherapy
takeaway: Established single-agent pembrolizumab as first-line standard for PD-L1-high NSCLC — chemotherapy-free treatment with better survival. Long-term follow-up shows a ~30% 5-year survival plateau.

name: KEYNOTE-042
population: Treatment-naive advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥1%, any histology.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs platinum chemotherapy
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: Extended the KEYNOTE-024 question down to TPS ≥1%. Worth filling in the numbers — the key nuance is that the apparent benefit at TPS 1–49% is largely driven by the TPS ≥50% subgroup.

name: KEYNOTE-045
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma after 1–2 prior lines, ECOG 0–2.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine)
