takeaway: Classic ICI pattern — PFS flat or worse, OS clearly better through durable responses. Established pembrolizumab as second-line standard in urothelial carcinoma. Watch the early non-responders who progress fast.

name: KEYNOTE-048
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC; PD within 6 months of CCRT excluded. Oral cavity 30%, oropharynx 40%, hypopharynx 13%, larynx 25%. TPS ≥50% ~20%; CPS ≥1 ~85%; p16+ 20%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab alone vs pembrolizumab + platinum + 5-FU vs EXTREME
endpoints: Pembro alone 16.9% vs. EXTREME 36.0%; pembro+ChT 36.3% vs. 36.3%
takeaway: Pembrolizumab alone improved OS in CPS ≥1 and is less toxic, but did not improve PFS or ORR. Pembrolizumab + chemo gave OS and ORR benefit in all patients, with a PFS benefit only in CPS ≥20.

name: KEYNOTE-177
population: Treatment-naive dMMR/MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer. 60% right-sided, 40% RAS/BRAF-mutant.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy (investigator's choice ± bevacizumab/cetuximab)
endpoints: ⚠️ 30% progressed as best response on pembrolizumab
takeaway: Made first-line pembrolizumab standard for dMMR mCRC, with a remarkable 77-month median OS. But 30% have primary resistance and progress immediately — RAS/BRAF-mutant patients may still need chemotherapy, which is the gap CheckMate-8HW's dual blockade addresses.

name: KEYNOTE-181
population: ESCC 64% / adenocarcinoma 36%; one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy. Asia 39%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 in 35%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w ×2 yr vs taxane or irinotecan (open-label)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab improved OS over chemotherapy only in CPS ≥10 (FDA approved in CPS ≥10); the SCC and all-comers co-primary OS endpoints did not meet their boundaries. This contrasts with ATTRACTION-3, where the OS benefit was regardless of PD-L1.

name: KEYNOTE-189
population: Treatment-naive metastatic NON-SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level, no EGFR/ALK alteration.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + pemetrexed/platinum vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The trial that established chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard for non-squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in the numbers.

name: KEYNOTE-224/240
population: HCC, Child-Pugh A, BCLC B–C.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=278) vs placebo (n=135)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab versus placebo in 2L HCC showed numerical OS and PFS gains that did not cross the significance boundaries, along with a notable ORR of 18.3%. Accelerated approval was maintained (ODAC 2021) even though KEYNOTE-240 failed, and it was confirmed later by KEYNOTE-394.

name: KEYNOTE-355
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, NO CPS requirement for entry. DFI 6–12 mo 20%, >12 mo 50%; de novo metastatic 30%; brain mets 2–6%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + chemo vs placebo + chemo
takeaway: First-line pembrolizumab + chemo improves both PFS and OS — but only at CPS ≥10. Below that, nothing. The sharp contrast with KEYNOTE-522 in early TNBC (where PD-L1 didn't matter at all) is one of the most instructive discrepancies in breast oncology.

name: KEYNOTE-394
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Asian countries, HBV (+); progression on or intolerance to sorafenib.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=300) vs placebo (n=153)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab improved OS, PFS and ORR over placebo in 2L Asian HCC after progression on or intolerance to sorafenib. It confirms the KEYNOTE-240 signal in an Asian, HBV-predominant population.

name: KEYNOTE-407
population: Treatment-naive metastatic SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/taxane vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The squamous counterpart to KEYNOTE-189, establishing chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in.

name: KEYNOTE-590
population: Both ESCC (73%) and adenocarcinoma (27%). Asia 53%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 in 51%; HER2-positive excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg + cisplatin/5-FU (PF) vs placebo + PF; double-blind, 1:1, N=749
takeaway: Pembrolizumab plus PF improved PFS, OS and ORR in first-line ESCC/EAC and is standard of care. The benefit is driven by CPS ≥10, and CPS <10 is essentially flat (HR 0.86).

name: LEAP-002
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C. Asian 40%; VP4 excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + lenvatinib vs lenvatinib
takeaway: Adding pembrolizumab to lenvatinib improved OS and PFS numerically but missed the prespecified significance threshold in first-line unresectable HCC. The lenvatinib control arm was strong (mOS 19.0 months), and the combination was more toxic.

name: MAINTAIN
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (86.5% palbociclib). ≤1 prior chemo line. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy + ribociclib vs switched ET + placebo (NSAI → fulvestrant or exemestane)
takeaway: Switching both the endocrine partner AND the CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib → ribociclib) retains benefit after progression — the first randomised evidence for CDK4/6 inhibitor beyond progression. Benefit was significant in ESR1 wild-type; prior CDK4/6i duration ≤12 months may still leave room.

name: MARIPOS
population: EGFR Ex19del (60%) or L858R (40%). Stable brain mets 40%; regular brain MRI; crossover prohibited.
treatment: Amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib vs lazertinib; chemo-free
takeaway: Amivantamab + lazertinib showed PFS and OS benefit in 1L EGFR-mutant NSCLC in a chemo-free regimen. Watch for toxicity.

name: MARIPOSA-2
population: EGFR Ex19del or L858R NSCLC progressing on or after osimertinib. Stable brain metastases allowed.
treatment: Amivantamab + chemo (± lazertinib) vs chemotherapy alone
endpoints: ⚠️ 17.7 vs 15.3 mo — numerically higher, not mature
takeaway: Addresses the hardest question in EGFR NSCLC — what to do after osimertinib. Amivantamab + chemo improves PFS, ORR and intracranial PFS. Costs: VTE, haematologic and skin toxicity.

name: MetaGIST
population: Unresectable or metastatic GIST on first-line imatinib. Pooled individual-patient data from two phase III trials (EORTC 62005 and SWOG S0033). Median follow-up 45 months; mutation data in 772 patients.
treatment: Imatinib 800 mg/d vs 400 mg/d, first line
takeaway: Upfront high-dose imatinib buys only a small early PFS advantage and no survival benefit — 400 mg remains the standard starting dose. The single exception is KIT exon 9-mutant GIST, where 800 mg more than doubles response rate.

name: ML18147 (TML)
population: mCRC progressing after first-line bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy. Sidedness not analysed. First line was not anti-EGFR.
treatment: Bevacizumab BEYOND progression + second-line chemo vs chemo alone
takeaway: Continuing bevacizumab past progression with a changed chemotherapy backbone improves survival — regardless of tumour sidedness. Established 'bev beyond progression' as a legitimate strategy.

name: MONALEESA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Ribociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Ribociclib + letrozole delivers both PFS and OS benefit first-line, with median OS exceeding 5 years. Notably, ribociclib has shown OS benefit where palbociclib has not.

name: MONALEESA-3
population: Postmenopausal HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. Half first-line (de novo or relapse >12 mo); half second-line (early relapse ≤12 mo or progression on ET), all CDK4/6i-naive.
treatment: Ribociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Ribociclib works with fulvestrant as well as with an AI, and the OS benefit holds in both first and second line. First-line PFS of 33.6 months is the standout figure.

name: MONALEESA-7
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. One prior line of chemotherapy allowed. The only CDK4/6 trial dedicated to this group.
treatment: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy + ovarian function suppression vs placebo + ET + OFS
takeaway: The only CDK4/6 inhibitor trial designed specifically for premenopausal women, and it delivered both PFS and OS benefit — nearly doubling PFS.

name: MONARCH-2
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy but CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance in ~25%.
treatment: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant improves PFS and OS after endocrine progression, delaying the move to chemotherapy by well over a year.

name: MONARCH-3
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Abemaciclib + non-steroidal AI vs placebo + NSAI
takeaway: Doubles first-line PFS, and the 13-month numerical OS gain narrowly missed significance. Side effects differ from the other CDK4/6 inhibitors: diarrhoea and VTE dominate over neutropenia.

name: MORPHEUS-Liver
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C. Asian 40%.
treatment: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab (A+B) + tiragolumab (n=40) vs A+B (n=18)
takeaway: Adding the anti-TIGIT antibody tiragolumab to A+B improved ORR, PFS and OS in this phase Ib/II study of first-line unresectable HCC. The numbers are small (40 vs 18) and the control arm underperformed, and the confirmatory IMbrave152/SKYSCRAPER-14 trial failed.

name: MOUNTAINEER
population: RAS wild-type, HER2-positive chemorefractory mCRC. Median 2–3 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (vs tucatinib alone)
takeaway: Tucatinib + trastuzumab is active and well tolerated in HER2+ RAS wild-type refractory mCRC — a 24-month median OS in a heavily pretreated population. Led to FDA approval.

name: MVAC (Loehrer)
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-eligible.
treatment: MVAC vs single-agent cisplatin
takeaway: The trial that established combination chemotherapy in urothelial carcinoma — more than tripling response rate over single-agent cisplatin. The foundation everything since has been measured against.

name: MyPathway (HER2 CRC cohort)
population: HER2-amplified mCRC, median 4 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Trastuzumab + pertuzumab (single-arm basket)
takeaway: Dual HER2 antibody blockade is active and well tolerated in HER2-amplified mCRC, particularly in KRAS wild-type. The short PFS reflects how heavily pretreated these patients were.

name: NALA
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer after ≥2 prior HER2-directed regimens. ECOG 0–1, 59% HR+, 84% visceral, 16.6% baseline brain mets. Prior: 99.7% trastuzumab, 42% pertuzumab, 54% T-DM1.
treatment: Neratinib + capecitabine vs lapatinib + capecitabine
endpoints: ✅ Fewer CNS interventions 22.8% vs 29.2%, P=0.043; DoR 8.5 vs 5.6 mo
takeaway: The first TKI-versus-TKI superiority trial in metastatic breast cancer. Note the tell-tale pattern — identical median PFS but separated mean PFS, meaning the benefit is in the tail. Grade 3 diarrhoea in 24% despite prophylaxis.

name: NO16966
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG ≤1.
treatment: Bevacizumab + oxaliplatin-based chemo (FOLFOX4 or XELOX) vs chemo alone
takeaway: Bevacizumab improved PFS but not OS or response rate with an oxaliplatin backbone — a weaker effect than with irinotecan. A key subtlety: many patients stopped bevacizumab early for chemo toxicity, which is why the trial argues for continuing bevacizumab until progression.

name: NSABP-B27 (real-world, Jordan)
population: 346 women with high-risk early breast cancer treated neoadjuvantly in Jordan 2003–2014. Median tumour 6.0 cm; 78.3% node-positive — notably more advanced than the original B-27 trial.
treatment: AC ×4 → docetaxel ×4 (single arm)
takeaway: Real-world outcomes matched the trial (pCR 25% vs 26%) despite larger tumours and far more nodal involvement. HR-negative, node-negative and smaller tumours predicted higher pCR. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an early-stage neoadjuvant study — it may belong in the Early DB.

name: OlympiAD
population: Germline BRCA1/2-mutant, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, ≤2 prior metastatic chemo lines. Prior anthracycline and taxane required; prior platinum for metastatic disease EXCLUDED.
treatment: Olaparib vs physician's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First PARP inhibitor trial in breast cancer — PFS benefit, no OS. But an OS signal in the chemotherapy-naive subgroup pointed toward earlier use, which is exactly what OlympiA went on to prove in the adjuvant setting.

name: P025
population: Postmenopausal advanced breast cancer, HR-positive (65%) or unknown (35%). Prior adjuvant endocrine therapy allowed.
treatment: Letrozole vs tamoxifen, first-line for advanced disease
takeaway: Established aromatase inhibitors over tamoxifen as first-line endocrine therapy in advanced disease — the metastatic counterpart to ATAC and BIG 1-98.

name: PALOMA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Palbociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Palbociclib clearly extends PFS but — unlike ribociclib in MONALEESA-2 — never delivered an OS benefit. The central unexplained puzzle of the CDK4/6 class. Main toxicity is myelosuppression.

name: PALOMA-3
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy, CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance ~21%.
treatment: Palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Doubles PFS after endocrine progression. The OS story is subgroup-dependent: no ITT benefit, but a large one in endocrine-sensitive patients — prior endocrine sensitivity predicts who gains.

name: PAOLA-1
population: FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer, regardless of surgical outcome or HRD status. CR 20%, stage III 70%, BRCA-mutant 30%, HRD+ ~50%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID ×2 years + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg Q3W ×15 mo vs placebo + bevacizumab
takeaway: Olaparib + bevacizumab maintenance after first-line bevacizumab-taxane/platinum improved PFS and OS in HRD-positive ovarian cancer, and is the only PARP inhibitor with an OS benefit. There was no benefit in HRD-negative disease.

name: PARADIGM
population: RAS wild-type mCRC, ECOG 0–1, prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded. Primary analysis in LEFT-SIDED tumours.
treatment: Panitumumab vs bevacizumab, both with mFOLFOX6
takeaway: The definitive prospective answer to the sidedness question — anti-EGFR first in LEFT-sided RAS wild-type disease, anti-VEGF for right-sided. Depth of response correlated with better OS.

name: PARSIFAL
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, ENDOCRINE-SENSITIVE, no prior treatment for advanced disease. Prior perioperative ET allowed if DFS >12 months.
treatment: Fulvestrant + palbociclib vs letrozole + palbociclib
endpoints: ❌ 27.9 vs 32.8 mo — HR 1.13 (0.89–1.45), P=0.32 — superiority NOT shown
takeaway: Fulvestrant is not a better CDK4/6 partner than an aromatase inhibitor in endocrine-sensitive first-line disease. Keep the NSAI.

name: postMONARCH
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (60% palbociclib), in either the advanced or early setting. Prior metastatic chemotherapy excluded. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy (AI → fulvestrant) + abemaciclib vs switched ET + placebo
takeaway: Confirms in phase III what MAINTAIN suggested — CDK4/6 inhibition beyond progression works, without biomarker selection. Unlike MAINTAIN, prior CDK4/6i duration did not affect the benefit. Be realistic about magnitude: the median PFS gain is under a month.

name: PRIME
population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC, ECOG ≤2. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4
takeaway: Panitumumab + FOLFOX improves both PFS and OS — but only in fully RAS wild-type tumours. The extended RAS analysis of this trial is what expanded testing beyond KRAS exon 2.

name: PYNNACLE
population: Solid tumours carrying the TP53 Y220C mutation (ovary, pancreas, breast, CRC, endometrial, lung, HEENT and others). ECOG 0–1, median 3 prior lines.
treatment: Rezatapopt (PC14586), an oral selective p53 reactivator (single-arm)
endpoints: 20% overall; 30% in KRAS wild-type at ≥1150 mg
takeaway: Proof of concept that a mutant p53 protein can be pharmacologically reactivated — a target considered undruggable for decades. RP2D 2000 mg daily with food; main toxicities GI and anaemia.

name: RAINBOW
population: Metastatic gastric or EGJ adenocarcinoma (EGJ 20%), adenocarcinoma only. Prior platinum-fluoropyrimidine. Asian 34%; peritoneal metastases 47%.
treatment: Ramucirumab + paclitaxel vs placebo + paclitaxel; no crossover
takeaway: Ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved PFS, OS and ORR in second-line metastatic gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma, making it the only antiangiogenic to succeed in GC/EGJ. The benefit was larger in the EGJ (adenocarcinoma) subgroup.

name: RASolute 302
population: Metastatic PDAC, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 prior fluoropyrimidine/gemcitabine chemotherapy, RAS-mutant (RAS G12X ~100%). Asian ~10%; ECOG 0 50%.
treatment: Daraxonrasib 300 mg PO QD vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (IOC ChT)
takeaway: Daraxonrasib beat chemotherapy on PFS, OS and ORR in second-line-or-later metastatic PDAC. A median OS of 13.2 months in this setting is the headline result.

name: RATIONALE-301
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; VP4 status not specified.
treatment: Tislelizumab vs sorafenib (non-inferiority design)
takeaway: Tislelizumab was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in 1L unresectable HCC, with worse PFS. It had a higher ORR and far fewer grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events.

name: RATIONALE-302
population: ESCC only, 1 prior line of chemo; 79% Asia; PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 31%.
treatment: Tislelizumab 200 mg q3w vs taxane or irinotecan (open-label, 1:1, N=512)
endpoints: ⚠️ 1.6 vs 2.1 mo — HR 0.83 (0.67–1.01); but 12-mo PFS 12.7% vs 1.9% (curves separate after ~3 mo)
takeaway: Tislelizumab improved OS over chemotherapy in 2L ESCC, while PFS was not significant. The benefit is concentrated in PD-L1-positive (TAP ≥10%) patients.

name: RATIONALE-306
population: ESCC only; 75% Asian; 44% had prior definitive therapy; PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 34%.
treatment: Tislelizumab + chemotherapy (PF or TP) vs placebo + chemotherapy; double-blind 1:1
takeaway: Tislelizumab + chemotherapy improved PFS, OS and ORR in 1L ESCC. The benefit is driven by patients with TAP ≥10%; in TAP <10% the OS signal was weaker and not clearly significant.

name: RATIONALE-309
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC; all Asian, China only. Liver metastases ~40%; baseline EBV-positive ~80%; 75% with prior CCRT.
treatment: Tislelizumab + GP vs placebo + GP; induction then maintenance; crossover 49%
endpoints: 69.5% vs 55.3% by BICR; 77.9% vs 67.4% by investigator
takeaway: Tislelizumab added to gemcitabine-cisplatin improved PFS in first-line recurrent/metastatic NPC, but OS was not significant, with 49% crossover. The row notes it as the only TFDA-approved option.

name: FOLFOXIRI — GONO
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 62. ECOG 0–1 in 98% — a deliberately FIT population.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (oxaliplatin 85, irinotecan 165, infusional 5-FU 46 h)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy improves response, PFS and OS — but only in genuinely fit patients (98% were ECOG 0–1). Patient selection is the whole story; see the HORG trial for what happens without it.

name: FOLFOXIRI — HORG
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 66, age ≥75 permitted. ECOG 0 in only 36%, ECOG 2 in 11%. Crossover allowed.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (lower doses: oxaliplatin 65, irinotecan 150, bolus 5-FU)
takeaway: The negative mirror image of the GONO trial — an older, less fit population, lower drug doses and bolus 5-FU produced no benefit and heavy toxicity. Together the two trials define exactly who FOLFOXIRI is for.

name: REACH-2
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C, AFP >400, progressing on sorafenib.
treatment: Ramucirumab (n=197) vs placebo (n=95)
takeaway: Ramucirumab improved OS and PFS over placebo in second-line HCC with AFP ≥400. REACH-1 in all-comers was negative, so the benefit is restricted to AFP ≥400.

name: RECOURSE
population: Refractory mCRC, median 3 prior regimens, 20% prior regorafenib. ECOG 0 in ~56%.
treatment: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) vs placebo
takeaway: Established TAS-102 as a third-line option in refractory mCRC. Like regorafenib, the benefit is real but small — disease stabilisation rather than response.

name: REFLECT
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; excluded Vp4, bile duct invasion and tumour >50% liver occupation.
treatment: Lenvatinib (n=478) vs sorafenib (n=476); non-inferiority design
takeaway: Lenvatinib was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in first-line unresectable HCC and improved PFS and ORR. The trial excluded Vp4, bile duct invasion and ≥50% liver occupation, so it should not be applied to those patients.

name: RESORCE
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1; progression on sorafenib (had to tolerate sorafenib).
treatment: Regorafenib (n=379) vs placebo (n=194)
takeaway: Regorafenib improved OS and PFS versus placebo in 2L HCC after sorafenib and was the first 2L approval. It only enrolled patients who tolerated sorafenib.

name: ReTrITA
population: Refractory mCRC after ≥2 prior lines.
treatment: Sequencing study — regorafenib → TAS-102 vs TAS-102 → regorafenib
endpoints: ✅ 11.5 vs 8.5 mo — HR 0.60 (0.49–0.74), P<0.0001 (monotherapy PFS nearly identical: 3.2 vs 3.3 mo)
takeaway: Sequence matters — regorafenib first, then TAS-102. Note the tell: each drug's individual PFS is identical, so the benefit comes from the ordering, not from either agent. Retrospective, so treat with appropriate caution.

name: RIGHT Choice
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with aggressive HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer — including visceral crisis — with no prior treatment for advanced disease. The population clinicians reflexively give chemotherapy.
treatment: Ribociclib + NSAI + ovarian function suppression vs investigator's-choice combination chemotherapy
takeaway: Directly challenges the instinct to reach for chemotherapy in visceral crisis — endocrine therapy plus ribociclib gave 9 months more PFS with better tolerability. Practice-changing for aggressive premenopausal HR+ disease.

name: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib, CRC)
population: RAS-mutant refractory colorectal cancer (details not yet captured).
treatment: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib) — RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for the colorectal cohort of daraxonrasib. Worth filling in — the same drug produced a doubling of OS in pancreatic cancer (RASolute 302).

name: Saltz et al.
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age ~60. Over half were ECOG 1–2; 80% had liver metastases.
treatment: Irinotecan + 5-FU/LV (IFL) vs 5-FU/LV vs irinotecan alone
takeaway: The trial that moved metastatic colorectal cancer from single-agent fluorouracil to doublet chemotherapy, lifting response rates from ~20% to 50%. The starting point of the modern mCRC treatment sequence.

name: SERENA-6
population: ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with an EMERGENT ESR1 mutation detected on ctDNA surveillance during first-line AI + CDK4/6i (≥6 months), with NO radiographic progression yet. A genuinely novel entry criterion.
treatment: Switch to camizestrant + continue the same CDK4/6 inhibitor vs continue AI + CDK4/6i
takeaway: The first trial to act on a molecular relapse before it becomes a radiographic one — switching endocrine partner on emergent ESR1 ctDNA nearly doubles PFS while keeping the CDK4/6 inhibitor. A new treatment paradigm, though OS is not yet known.

name: SHARP
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤2; >80% from Europe and Australasia.
treatment: Sorafenib (n=299) vs placebo (n=303)
takeaway: Sorafenib improved OS and PFS over placebo in first-line advanced HCC and became the first systemic standard of care. ORR was about 0%, so the benefit comes from stable disease (DCR 43% vs 32%).

name: SOFT (adjuvant)
population: Pre/perimenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer — adjuvant setting.
treatment: Tamoxifen alone vs tamoxifen + OFS vs exemestane + OFS
takeaway: High-risk premenopausal women benefit from ovarian function suppression. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an adjuvant trial, and largely duplicates the SOFT/TEXT entry in your Early DB — worth consolidating.

name: SOHO-01
population: HER2-mutant NSCLC (details not yet captured).
treatment: Sevabertinib (BAY 2927088) — HER2-selective TKI
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for sevabertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC — a sibling to zongertinib (Beamion Lung-01). Worth filling both in together for comparison.

name: SOLAR1
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer in men and postmenopausal women, relapsed/progressed on an AI; no chemo in the advanced setting; prior CDK4/6i 6%. Primary analysis in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort; patients with diabetes/poor glycaemic control excluded.
treatment: Alpelisib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Alpelisib + fulvestrant improved PFS but not OS in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after an AI. Bone-only disease appears to gain no benefit, and severe hyperglycemia is a key toxicity.

name: Sorafenib in desmoid tumour
population: Progressive, symptomatic or recurrent desmoid tumours. Median age 37, 69% female, 40% prior systemic therapy, 50% prior surgery. Crossover allowed at progression.
treatment: Sorafenib 400 mg daily vs placebo
endpoints: ✅ 33% vs 20% — median time to response 9.6 mo
takeaway: First randomised phase III in desmoid tumours, with a striking 87% reduction in progression risk. Two clinical lessons: responses are late (median 9.6 months) so don't abandon stable disease early, and the 20% placebo response rate supports watchful waiting as a first move. 20% discontinued for skin toxicity.

name: STELLAR-303
population: MSS/pMMR refractory mCRC — a true third line: all had received 5-FU, irinotecan and oxaliplatin; no prior regorafenib, TAS-102 or ICI; BRAF-mutant required prior BRAF-targeted therapy.
treatment: Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab vs regorafenib
takeaway: Immunotherapy finally shows an OS signal in MSS colorectal cancer — but with a modest 1.5-month gain and substantially more toxicity. Weigh carefully in a late-line population.

name: SUNLIGHT
population: Refractory mCRC — >90% had exactly 2 prior lines. ECOG 0 in 43–48%.
treatment: TAS-102 + bevacizumab vs TAS-102 alone
endpoints: ✅ No prior bev HR 0.40 vs prior bev HR 0.72
takeaway: Adding bevacizumab to TAS-102 more than doubles PFS and gives a 3.3-month OS gain — the best third-line result in mCRC. Benefit is much larger in bevacizumab-naive patients.

name: TRIBE
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~90%; right-sided 25–35%.
treatment: Bevacizumab + FOLFOXIRI (triplet) vs bevacizumab + FOLFIRI (doublet)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab improves OS in fit patients. Subgroup analysis supports it particularly for right-sided tumours, where anti-EGFR does not work.

name: TRIBE2
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~85%; right-sided 40%.
treatment: Upfront bevacizumab-triplet (with reintroduction after progression) vs sequential bevacizumab-doublet
takeaway: Confirms TRIBE with a strategy endpoint — giving the triplet upfront, then reintroducing it, beats sequential doublets on PFS2 and OS. Particularly relevant for right-sided disease.

name: TriComB
population: UNFIT, elderly mCRC — median age 80, ECOG 1 in ~55%, RAS-mutant ~80%.
treatment: TAS-102 + capecitabine + bevacizumab
takeaway: A chemo-light triplet for patients too frail for standard doublets — 55% response and 10 months PFS at a median age of 80 is a strong early signal. Randomised confirmation pending.

name: TRIPLETE
population: RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC, left-sided 88%, ECOG 0 in ~80%. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOXIRI vs panitumumab + FOLFOX
endpoints: ✅ 41.1 vs 33.3 mo — HR 0.79 (0.63–0.99), P=0.049 — inconsistent with the primary result
takeaway: In RAS/BRAF wild-type disease, anti-EGFR plus a doublet is already good enough — the triplet adds toxicity without improving response or PFS. Treat the borderline OS finding with scepticism given the negative primary endpoint.

name: TROPION-Breast02
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, ICI-INELIGIBLE. No DFI requirement — deliberately includes the worst-prognosis first-line patients: DFI 0–6 mo 15%, de novo 34%, brain mets 10%.
treatment: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First-line Dato-DXd improves BOTH PFS and OS in ICI-ineligible metastatic TNBC — and did so in a deliberately poor-prognosis population (the highest brain-met and short-DFI proportions of any first-line TNBC trial). Sits alongside ASCENT-03 as the answer for CPS <10 disease.

name: VIKTORIA-1
population: HR+/HER2− PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer with progression on CDK4/6i + NSAI.
treatment: Gedatolisib + fulvestrant ± palbociclib vs fulvestrant (open-label)
endpoints: ✅ 9.3 (triplet) vs 7.4 (doublet) vs 2.0 (fulvestrant) mo — HR triplet 0.24 (0.17–0.35), p<0.001; HR doublet 0.33 (0.24–0.48), p<0.001
takeaway: In PIK3CA wild-type HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6i + NSAI, gedatolisib plus fulvestrant with or without palbociclib improved PFS, with OS not significant. The triplet was associated with neutropenia.

name: ATTRACTION-5
population: Pathological stage IIIA–C gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after gastrectomy with D2+ lymph-node dissection. Asian only (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China).
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab added to chemotherapy did not improve RFS after D2 gastrectomy for stage III gastric/GEJ cancer. It is the first phase 3 of adjuvant ICI after D2 surgery in Asia and it is negative, in contrast with the perioperative approaches tested in KEYNOTE-585 and MATTERHORN. The nivolumab arm paid for it in toxicity — endocrine adverse events 21% vs 3% and more discontinuations — with no efficacy in return.

name: CheckMate-141
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC progressing within 6 months of platinum given either as adjuvant therapy or as first-line treatment for metastatic disease. Oral cavity 50%, oropharynx 35%, larynx 14%. Prior cetuximab 62%, ≥2 prior lines 55%, PD-L1 ≥1% 57%.
treatment: Nivolumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab), randomised 2:1
takeaway: Nivolumab monotherapy improves overall survival in platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic HNSCC without improving PFS — the gain is in the tail of the curve, not the early one. Benefit is concentrated in PD-L1-positive disease and vanishes below 1%. Its entry criteria were broader than KEYNOTE-040's: patients recurring within 3 months of definitive platinum-based therapy were eligible here.

name: CheckMate-238
population: R0 stage IIIB, IIIC or IV cutaneous melanoma (AJCC7; no IIIA); resected brain metastases allowed. IIIB 35%, IIIC 45%, IV ~20%; BRAF-mutant 40%.
treatment: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w vs ipilimumab 10 mg/kg IV q3w ×4 → q12w (both ≤1 year)
takeaway: One year of adjuvant nivolumab improved RFS and DMFS over ipilimumab and became standard of care. OS showed no difference, which the row attributes to the active comparator, and nivolumab was far less toxic than ipilimumab.

name: CheckMate-511
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 wks. Active brain mets excluded.
treatment: Nivolumab 3 + ipilimumab 1 ×4 vs nivolumab 1 + ipilimumab 3 ×4, then nivolumab 480 mg q4w maintenance
endpoints: 57.3% vs. 62.4% (CR+PR+SD; calculated, not reported as DCR in the paper)
takeaway: Supports flipping from nivolumab 1 + ipilimumab 3 (CheckMate-067) to nivolumab 3 + ipilimumab 1 for a better safety profile with similar efficacy. Efficacy endpoints are descriptive only, and there is no comparison to nivolumab monotherapy.

name: CheckMate-76K
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery; ocular and mucosal melanoma excluded. IIB 60%; superficial spreading 30%, nodular 50%, acral 5%; BRAF V600E-mutant 28–30%.
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg q4w × 1 yr vs placebo, randomised 2:1
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas COUNTED as RFS events and death COUNTED as a DMFS event — unlike KEYNOTE-716
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year more than halves the recurrence hazard in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, with a matching distant-metastasis benefit. There is still no OS report, and the price is real: 50% discontinued for adverse events and 15% needed hormone replacement for endocrine immune toxicity. Because it counts new primary melanomas as RFS events where KEYNOTE-716 does not, the two trials' hazard ratios are not directly comparable.

name: CheckMate-915
population: Completely resected stage IIIB–D or IV melanoma (AJCC 8th); complete lymph-node dissection NOT required. Cutaneous ~88%, acral ~3%, mucosal ~1%; stage IV 13%; BRAF-mutant 31%.
treatment: Nivolumab 240 mg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w vs nivolumab 480 mg q4w + placebo — both ≤1 year
endpoints: ⚠️ 2-yr 89.8% vs 91.8% — HR 1.09 (0.80–1.32), immature and numerically favours nivolumab alone
takeaway: Adding low-dose ipilimumab to adjuvant nivolumab failed both co-primary RFS endpoints and DMFS, with immature OS running numerically the wrong way — single-agent nivolumab, as in CheckMate-238, is enough. The one useful design lesson is that enrolling patients who had not had a completion lymph-node dissection did not degrade RFS.

name: COMBI-AD
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th) carrying a BRAF V600E (90%) or V600K mutation. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%.
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ 3-yr 86% vs 77% — HR 0.57 (0.42–0.79), P=0.0006 against a required P=0.000019, so not significant
takeaway: One year of adjuvant dabrafenib/trametinib halves the recurrence hazard and improves DMFS in resected BRAF V600-mutant stage III melanoma; OS improved numerically but never crossed the extremely stringent interim boundary. It makes targeted therapy a legitimate adjuvant option in BRAF-mutant disease — but DREAMseq later showed that in the metastatic setting ICI should come before BRAF/MEK inhibition.

name: DREAMseq
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III/IV melanoma with BRAF V600E/K mutation (V600E 82%, V600K 12%); prior adjuvant therapy 12-16%. No prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4 or BRAF/MEK therapy (even neo/adjuvant). Treated brain metastases allowed.
treatment: Sequence A/C: NIVO1-IPI3 first, then DABRA-TRAME after PD, vs Sequence B/D: DABRA-TRAME first, then NIVO-IPI after PD (NIVO-IPI followed by maintenance nivolumab)
takeaway: In BRAF V600-mutant melanoma, giving nivolumab-ipilimumab before RAF/MEK inhibition improved OS, duration of response and 2L ORR. The benefit comes from 2L: TKIs still work after dual ICI, but dual ICI works poorly in 2L. Only about 50% crossed over, so 1L treatment matters most.

name: EORTC 18071
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th); LDH >2× ULN excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%. BRAF status not prespecified.
treatment: Ipilimumab 10 mg/kg q3w ×4 then q12w for up to 3 years vs placebo
takeaway: The first adjuvant melanoma trial to show an overall survival benefit, proving that adjuvant checkpoint blockade can do more than delay recurrence. It is a landmark rather than a current option: high-dose ipilimumab was so toxic that the median patient received only 4 doses of a planned 3-year course, and it was superseded by adjuvant nivolumab in CheckMate-238.

name: EXTREME
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC with detectable EGFR expression.
treatment: Platinum + 5-FU + cetuximab (400 → 250 mg/m² weekly) vs platinum + 5-FU alone; chemotherapy q3w for up to 6 cycles
takeaway: Adding cetuximab to platinum/5-FU improved response, PFS and overall survival, making it the first-line standard of care in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC until KEYNOTE-048 displaced it. The cost is more sepsis and hypomagnesaemia.

name: INFINITY
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H, EBV-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (Italian GONO). Cohort 1 (n=18) cT≥2 any N M0 proceeds to surgery; cohort 2 (n=18) cT2–3 any N M0 goes to definitive non-operative management if a clinical CR is achieved (T4 excluded after cohort 1).
treatment: Chemo-free tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w ×3 (T300/D), single arm
endpoints: ⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Chemo-free neoadjuvant tremelimumab + durvalumab produced a 60% pCR and 80% major pathological response in resectable MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, reproducing NEONIPIGA. Cohort 2 provides the first prospective feasibility data for organ preservation in this disease — 76% reached a clinical CR and avoided surgery, with a single local regrowth salvaged surgically. T4 tumours respond far less well (pCR 17% vs 89%), linked to an M2-macrophage-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment, and are now excluded from the non-operative cohort.

name: INT-0099
population: Stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma (AJCC/UICC), no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, performance status 0–2.
treatment: Concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation → adjuvant cisplatin/5-FU vs radiotherapy alone
endpoints: ✅ NR vs 15 mo; 3-yr 66% vs 26% — HR 4.34 (2.47–7.69) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P<0.001
✅ NR vs 34 mo; 3-yr 76% vs 46% — HR 2.50 (1.29–4.84) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P=0.005
takeaway: The landmark trial that made concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation followed by adjuvant chemotherapy the standard of care in stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma, roughly doubling 3-year PFS and OS over radiotherapy alone. Read the hazard ratios carefully: they are expressed with radiotherapy alone in the numerator, so values above 1 favour chemoradiation.

name: KEYNOTE-585
population: Untreated, locally advanced, resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (T3 or deeper, or node-positive, M0). Global — 143 centres in 24 countries, 47% Asia.
treatment: Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy on a cisplatin/capecitabine or 5-FU backbone (separate FLOT safety cohort, n=203)
endpoints: ⚠️ 44.4 vs 25.3 mo — HR 0.81 (0.67–0.99), P=0.0198 against a boundary of P<0.0178, so not met; 2-yr EFS 58% vs 51%
takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab produced a large pCR gain but missed the prespecified EFS significance boundary by a hair (P=0.0198 vs the required 0.0178), and OS was not significant. It is the first global phase 3 of perioperative ICI in resectable gastric/GEJ cancer and a near-miss, contrasting with the subsequently positive MATTERHORN. The main cohort did not use FLOT as the chemotherapy backbone, which limits how far the result travels outside Asia.

name: KEYNOTE-040
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC progressing on platinum, or recurring within 3–6 months of platinum-based definitive therapy, a narrower population than CheckMate-141. Prior cetuximab 60%, ≥2 prior lines ~30%, PD-L1 ≥1% 80%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel, cetuximab); crossover 13%
takeaway: Pembrolizumab monotherapy improved OS but not PFS in platinum-refractory, PD-L1-positive HNSCC. Its population, recurrence within 3–6 months of definitive therapy, is narrower than that of CheckMate-141.

name: KEYNOTE-054
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th). IIIA 15%, IIIB 45%, IIIC 37%; BRAF V600-mutant 40–45%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 18 doses (~1 yr) vs placebo
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab became a standard of care in resected stage III melanoma, cutting the recurrence hazard by roughly 43% with a matching distant-metastasis benefit, and it works regardless of PD-L1 status. OS is still immature, and — unlike CheckMate-238 — no stage IV patients were enrolled, so the result does not extend to resected metastatic disease.

name: KEYNOTE-716
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery. IIB 65%. Histological subtype and BRAF status were deliberately not prespecified for subgroup analysis.
treatment: Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas NOT counted as RFS events and death NOT counted as a DMFS event — unlike CheckMate-76K
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab improves RFS and DMFS in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, the stage-II counterpart to CheckMate-76K. Check the endpoint definitions before comparing the two: this trial excluded new primary melanomas from RFS events and deaths from DMFS events, where CheckMate-76K counted both. OS is immature, and BRAF and PD-L1 subgroups were deliberately not prespecified.

name: NADINA
population: Stage IIIB–IIID melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease. Unknown primary 20%, in-transit metastases 10%; T2 20%, T3 20%, T4 25%; BRAF-mutant 50%.
treatment: Perioperative nivolumab 240 mg + ipilimumab 80 mg q3w ×2 → therapeutic lymph node dissection → response-driven therapy (nothing further after a major pathological response; dabrafenib/trametinib ×46 wk if BRAF-mutant, nivolumab ×11 if wild-type) vs adjuvant control (TLND → nivolumab 480 mg q4w ×12)
endpoints: ✅ pCR 47.2% + near-pCR 11.8% = MPR 59.0%; by BRAF, mutant 53.8% vs wild-type 65.3%; radiologic ORR at wk 6 35.8%
⏳ Blinded until the prespecified final analysis, 3 years after the last patient is enrolled
takeaway: Two cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab/ipilimumab before lymph node dissection cut the event hazard by two-thirds versus standard adjuvant nivolumab, and 59% of patients achieved a major pathological response and needed no further therapy at all. It also establishes pathological response as predictive of survival — 12-month RFS runs from 95% in major responders down to 57% in non-responders — which is what makes response-driven escalation and de-escalation possible. OS is still blinded.

name: NEONIPIGA
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2–T4 N0/1 M0, ECOG 0–1, age ≤75; French GERCOR study across 11 centres.
treatment: Neoadjuvant nivolumab + low-dose ipilimumab → surgery → adjuvant nivolumab (single arm)
endpoints: Not reached at 14.9-mo median follow-up; 30/31 (97%) eligible patients alive and event-free (1 postoperative death)
Not reached; 30/31 (97%) alive at data cutoff
⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab produced a 58.6% pCR in resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, far above the ~3–11% historically achieved with chemotherapy, with 100% R0 resection and manageable immune-related toxicity. It raised the question of a watch-and-wait, non-operative strategy for MSI-H gastric cancer, tested prospectively in INFINITY cohort 2. Neither PD-L1 CPS nor Lynch-versus-sporadic status predicted pathological response.

name: PRODIGY
population: Korean, ECOG 0–1, cT2–3 node-positive or cT4 any N gastric cancer (AJCC 7th). Stage III 80%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant DOS (docetaxel/oxaliplatin/S-1) ×3 → surgery → adjuvant S-1 vs surgery → adjuvant S-1
endpoints: 10.4% (23/222) in the neoadjuvant arm; not applicable to the surgery-first arm
⚠️ 3-yr 74.2% vs 73.4% — HR 0.84 (0.60–1.19), P=0.338; immature and underpowered
takeaway: The first Asian phase 3 to show that adding neoadjuvant chemotherapy to surgery plus adjuvant S-1 improves progression-free survival in locally advanced gastric cancer. The gain did not carry through to overall survival — the OS analysis was immature and underpowered — so it supports rather than proves the perioperative approach in a D2-gastrectomy population.

name: RELATIVITY-047
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III/IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 months ago. Active CNS metastases excluded. BRAF mutant 38%.
treatment: Relatlimab 160 mg + nivolumab 480 mg vs nivolumab Q4W
takeaway: Relatlimab + nivolumab improved PFS, ORR and OS over nivolumab alone in 1L melanoma, the first positive LAG-3 trial. PD-L1 was not predictive of efficacy.

name: SWOG S1801
population: Resectable stage IIIB–IIID or oligometastatic stage IV melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease (resectable node >1.5 cm short axis). Prior ICI and brain metastases excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 45%; acral 3%, mucosal 3%; BRAF-mutant ~25%.
treatment: Perioperative pembrolizumab ×3 → surgery → pembrolizumab ×15 vs surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab ×18 — 200 mg q3w, 18 total doses in both arms
endpoints: ⏳ Immature — 36 deaths in total (14 vs 22), too few for a definitive comparison
takeaway: Giving the same total amount of pembrolizumab but moving three doses in front of surgery improved 2-year event-free survival by over 20 percentage points. It is the proof of concept that neoadjuvant ICI beats purely adjuvant ICI — sequence, not dose or duration, is what changed. OS is still immature.

name: CheckMate-067
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 wks. Active brain mets excluded. BRAF-mutant 31.5%.
treatment: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w vs nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + placebo vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 + placebo
takeaway: Nivolumab alone and nivolumab + ipilimumab both beat ipilimumab alone on PFS, OS and ORR in metastatic melanoma. The combination is significantly more toxic.

name: ARASENS
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC); prior treatment not allowed. Visceral mets 17%.
treatment: Darolutamide 600 mg BID + ADT + docetaxel (triplet) vs placebo + ADT + docetaxel
takeaway: Adding darolutamide to ADT + docetaxel improved OS and the other secondary endpoints, so a patient fit for docetaxel should be offered first-line triplet therapy. Watch for cardiac disorders as an adverse effect.

name: ARCHES
population: mHSPC; 63% high-volume disease, Gleason ≥8 in 67%. Prior therapy allowed: docetaxel 18%, ADT ≤3 mo 72%, ADT >3 mo 20%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Enzalutamide added to ADT improved rPFS, OS and the other secondary endpoints in mHSPC, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Watch for side effects: hypertension and CNS effects (fatigue, cognitive decline).

name: CHAARTED
population: Treatment-naive mHSPC; prior adjuvant ADT allowed if completed ≥12 mo earlier. Prespecified high-volume disease (visceral mets, or ≥4 bone mets with ≥1 non-axial) ~65%; ~60% Gleason ≥8; 75% de novo.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel vs ADT alone; docetaxel 75 mg/m2 Q3W ×6
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT in high-volume mHSPC improved OS and time to CRPC. The benefit was not observed in low-volume disease.

name: ENZAMET
population: mHSPC; high-volume 52%, Gleason ≥8 60%. Prior therapy allowed: planned early docetaxel 45%, anti-androgen 50%, ADT 70%.
treatment: Enzalutamide + ADT (± early docetaxel) vs standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide/nilutamide/flutamide) + ADT (± early docetaxel)
endpoints: ⚠️ No early docetaxel planned HR 0.53 (0.37–0.75); early docetaxel planned HR 0.90 (0.62–1.31)
takeaway: Enzalutamide + ADT improved OS and clinical PFS, along with other secondary endpoints, versus first-generation anti-androgens in mHSPC. Caveat: the OS benefit was attenuated in the planned early docetaxel subgroup.

name: CAPItello-281
population: PTEN-deficient de novo mHSPC; high-risk 60%, high-volume 74%, Gleason ≥8 ~80%. No prior chemotherapy; prior abiraterone ~10% allowed.
treatment: Capivasertib 400 mg BID (4 days on, 3 off) + abiraterone + ADT vs placebo + abiraterone + ADT
takeaway: Adding capivasertib to abiraterone + ADT improved rPFS and other secondary endpoints in PTEN-loss metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. OS is immature (26.4% maturity), and side effects include hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea and rash.

name: GETUG-AFU 15
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive (non-castrate) prostate cancer, N=385 (192 vs 193). Metastatic at initial diagnosis 67% (docetaxel arm) / 75% (ADT-alone); median age 63–64; bone metastases 81%.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel vs ADT alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT did not improve OS (HR 1.01), unlike CHAARTED, even though all secondary endpoints improved (biochemical PFS, clinical PFS, PSA response). OS was confounded by crossover: 62% of the ADT-alone arm got docetaxel at castration resistance vs 28% re-treated in the docetaxel arm. Median OS was longer than historical series in both arms (54–59 months), suggesting the trial may have been underpowered for its assumed effect size.

name: LATITUDE
population: High-risk treatment-naive mHSPC (≥2 of 3: Gleason ≥8, ≥3 bone mets, visceral mets); prior therapy not allowed. 96% had Gleason ≥8 plus ≥3 bone mets.
treatment: Abiraterone + prednisone + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Adding abiraterone + prednisone to ADT improved rPFS and OS, as well as the other key secondary endpoints, in high-risk mHSPC. Watch for mineralocorticoid excess (hypertension, hypokalemia).

name: PEACE-1
population: De novo mHSPC; 60.6% received docetaxel; 43.1% low-volume (CHAARTED criteria).
treatment: 2×2 factorial: SOC (ADT ± docetaxel) ± abiraterone, ± prostate RT (74 Gy/37 fr)
endpoints: rPFS (1°), low-volume, AAP+RT vs AAP alone
rPFS (1°), low-volume, RT vs no RT (no AAP)
rPFS (1°), ITT, AAP+RT vs abiraterone alone
OS (1°), ITT, pooled RT vs no RT
takeaway: The only scenario in which adding RT improved rPFS was RT plus abiraterone (AAP) in low-volume disease, and adding RT delayed progression to CRPC. There was no overall OS benefit from RT.

name: INT-0162 (SWOG S9346)
population: Treatment-naive mHSPC, ECOG 0–2. Gleason ≥8 ~20%, visceral metastases 6–7%, extensive disease ~50%.
treatment: Non-inferiority design: 7-mo ADT + bicalutamide, randomized if PSA ≤4 → continuous ADT vs intermittent ADT (resume ADT when PSA ≥20 or back to baseline; stop again after 7 mo once PSA ≤4)
endpoints: ⚠️ Statistically inconclusive: HR 1.10 (0.99–1.23), boundary 1.2 → cannot state that iADT was significantly inferior to cADT
takeaway: Intermittent ADT appeared non-inferior to continuous ADT, but the non-inferiority margin was not statistically met. Continuous ADT therefore remained SOC.

name: HERO
population: Mixed population: 31.7% metastatic (22.7% de novo), 50.2% relapsed non-metastatic, 27.1% locally advanced.
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide
endpoints: ✅ 96.7% vs 88.8% (+7.9%) through 48 wk, testosterone <50 ng/dL; P<0.001 for superiority
NA (trial did not assess oncologic efficacy)
takeaway: Oral relugolix achieved higher sustained castration and a lower MACE rate (about 54% lower by HR) than the GnRH agonist leuprolide. The trial did not assess oncologic efficacy, and the population was mixed.

name: HERO
population: Cross-listed from the Metastatic Cancer Database because the population spans multiple disease settings (flagged in Notion). N=930 (622 vs 308): 50.2% biochemical/clinical relapse after curative local therapy (non-metastatic), 27.1% advanced localized disease unsuitable for curative local intervention, 31.7% metastatic (22.7% newly diagnosed androgen-sensitive). >90% had cardiovascular risk factors.
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide (injectable LHRH agonist), both as ADT
endpoints: ✅ 96.7% vs 88.8% (testosterone <50 ng/dL through 48 wk) — difference 7.9 pts (95% CI 4.1–11.8); P<0.001 for superiority
takeaway: Oral relugolix gave rapid, sustained testosterone suppression that was superior to injectable leuprolide, with no testosterone surge (castrate by day 4 vs a surge to ~625 ng/dL with leuprolide). It was associated with a 54% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, most pronounced in patients with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors. Caveat: this is a head-to-head ADT-formulation trial with pharmacodynamic and cardiovascular endpoints, not a curative-intent treatment-intensification trial, and it did not assess oncologic efficacy.

name: STAMPEDE (Arm C)
population: Treatment-naive mHSPC; 76% assessable by CHAARTED definition (44% low-burden, 56% high-burden). ~70% Gleason ≥8; ~95% de novo.
treatment: SOC (ADT) + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV q3w ×6 + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs SOC (ADT) alone (2:1)
endpoints: ✅ Low-burden 93.2 vs 76.7; high-burden 39.9 vs 35.2 — no heterogeneity (interaction P=0.827)
takeaway: Docetaxel added to ADT improved OS in mHSPC regardless of metastatic burden, as compared with CHAARTED; STAMPEDE's low-burden subgroup was larger (n=362). It also improved FFS, PFS, mPFS and PCSS.

name: STAMPEDE (Arm G) — M1
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer from STAMPEDE Arm G (trial-wide 75% M1, 25% M0). Gleason ≥8 in 75%.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg QD + prednisolone 5 mg QD + ADT vs ADT alone
endpoints: ✅ HR 0.31 (0.26–0.37); trial-wide RMST over 54 mo 43.9 vs 30.0 (Δ13.9)
↔ None for OS or FFS (interaction P=0.37 OS, P=0.08 FFS)
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT improved both FFS and OS in this arm. Some figures given are trial-wide (M1 and M0 combined), and there was no heterogeneity of effect by metastatic status.

name: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M0
population: Newly diagnosed node-positive M0, or node-negative M0 high-risk locally advanced (≥2 of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL) prostate cancer starting long-term ADT, or relapsing after radical local therapy with high-risk features. Pre-specified M0 subgroup (n=915 of 1917). RT was mandatory for node-negative M0 and encouraged for node-positive M0; RT use ~39–40% in both arms.
treatment: ADT (SOC) + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg once daily vs ADT alone
endpoints: ⏳ HR 0.75 (0.48–1.18); deaths 34/460 (7%) vs 44/455 (10%); immature, only 78 deaths trial-wide in M0
↔ No heterogeneity: interaction P=0.37 for OS, P=0.08 for FFS
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT + RT improved FFS in the non-metastatic subgroup (HR 0.21), even though abiraterone was capped at 2 years. The OS signal (HR 0.75, 0.48–1.18) is favourable but immature, there was no heterogeneity vs the metastatic subgroup (companion M1 entry), and G3–5 AEs were more frequent (47% vs 33% trial-wide, mainly hypertension/hepatic).

name: TITAN
population: mHSPC; high-volume 63%. Prior treatment allowed: prior docetaxel 11%. Gleason ≥8 67%.
treatment: Apalutamide 240 mg/day + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Apalutamide + ADT improved rPFS and OS and the other secondary endpoints, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Adverse effects to note are rash, hypothyroidism and IHD.

name: ARTEMIS-008
population: SCLC after 1L chemotherapy. Stable brain mets 20%; prior ICI 80%; chemo-free interval <90 d in ~36%.
treatment: Risvutatug rezetecan 8 mg/kg Q3W vs topotecan 1.2 mg/m² D1–5 Q3W
takeaway: Risvutatug rezetecan improved PFS and OS over topotecan in 2L SCLC, and is the first B7-H3 ADC with an OS benefit. Interstitial lung disease and hematologic toxicity are the adverse effects to watch.

name: AFFIRM
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. ECOG 2 in 9%; visceral (liver/lung) mets in 23%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved both radiographic PFS and overall survival over placebo in mCRPC after docetaxel. The adverse effects to watch are fatigue and seizure.

name: COU-AA-301
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. ECOG 2 10%; bone mets ~89%, liver 10%; median PSA ~130.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisolone improved rPFS and OS versus placebo in mCRPC after docetaxel. Watch for mineralocorticoid-related side effects.

name: COU-AA-302
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC; no visceral metastases.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
endpoints: 98 vs 85 (derived as 100% − progressive disease%; not stated directly)
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisolone improved rPFS and OS over placebo + prednisolone in pre-docetaxel mCRPC. Caveats: visceral metastases were excluded, and the OS HR crossed the efficacy boundary only at the 4th interim analysis.

name: PREVAIL
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC; visceral mets allowed (~12%).
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved both rPFS and OS versus placebo in mCRPC before docetaxel. The trial included patients with visceral metastases.

name: MAGNITUDE
population: 1L mCRPC with HRD required. Prior ARPI for nmCRPC/mCSPC, or abiraterone up to 4 mo in mCRPC, allowed. BRCA1/2 subgroup 53%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg QD + abiraterone/prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone
takeaway: Niraparib plus abiraterone improved rPFS but not OS versus abiraterone alone in 1L HRR+ mCRPC. The benefit is concentrated in the BRCA subgroup.

name: PROfound
population: mCRPC with progression on enzalutamide or abiraterone; HRR mutation required. Cohort A: ≥1 mutation in BRCA1, BRCA2 or ATM; Cohort B: ≥1 mutation in 12 HRR genes. Visceral metastases 27%/35%; prior taxane 65%, prior abiraterone 40%, enzalutamide 40%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs investigator's-choice ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Olaparib monotherapy improved rPFS and OS in BRCA/ATM-mutant mCRPC after prior ARPI. Caveat: crossover was 81%.

name: PROpel
population: First-line mCRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutated ~28%; BRCA1 2%/1%, BRCA2 10%/9%. Visceral metastases ~12%; prior docetaxel ~22%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID + abiraterone/prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone
takeaway: Olaparib plus abiraterone improved ibPFS and PFS2 over abiraterone in first-line mCRPC regardless of HRR status, while OS is immature. Benefit is concentrated in HRR-mutated disease (HR 0.50 vs 0.76), and anemia and VTE were the adverse events noted.

name: TALAPRO-2
population: 1L mCRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutant 21%, BRCA1/2 7%; visceral metastases 14%; prior taxane 22%.
treatment: Talazoparib 0.5 mg QD + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide
endpoints: ✅ HRR+ 27.9 vs 16.4 mo; ⚠️ HRR- NR vs 22.5 mo
takeaway: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS versus enzalutamide alone in 1L mCRPC, with greater benefit in HRR+ disease. It carries significant hematologic adverse events, more than olaparib or niraparib.

name: TRITON2
population: mCRPC with BRCA mutation, n=115; PD after ARPI and taxane (median 2 prior CRPC treatments). BRCA1 n=13, BRCA2 n=71; germline n=44. Prior abiraterone 64.3%, enzalutamide 71.3%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID (single-arm phase 2)
takeaway: Rucaparib monotherapy gave an ORR of 43.5% in heavily pretreated BRCA1/2-mutant mCRPC. This is a single-arm study, so there is no comparator or HR, and OS is immature.

name: ROAR
cancer: BTC / HEENT / GIST / Other (BRAF V600E basket)
population: Previously treated advanced rare cancers with BRAF V600E; no prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor. N=206.
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD (single-arm basket, no control)
endpoints: ✅ Investigator-assessed: ATC 56%, BTC 53%, LGG 54%, HGG 33%, ASI 67% (2/3), HCL 89%, MM 50%, GIST 0% (1 pt, SD)
ATC 6.7, BTC 9.0, HGG 5.5, ASI 9.5, MM 6.3; LGG, HCL: NE
ATC 14.5, BTC 13.5, HGG 17.6, ASI 21.8, MM 33.9; LGG, HCL: NE
ATC 14.4, BTC 8.9, HGG 31.2, MM 11.1, ASI 7.7; LGG/HCL NR
takeaway: Dabrafenib + trametinib produced an ORR of about 50% in previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant rare cancers, in a single-arm phase II basket without a control arm. It supports an FDA tumor-agnostic approval for BRAF V600E-mutant cancers, with CRC excepted.

name: PSMAddition
population: PSMA-PET-positive mHSPC (no PSMA-negative lesion exclusion); treatment-naive or ≤45 d of ARPI/ADT (90%). High-volume 68%; de novo 50%; visceral (lung/liver) 15%.
treatment: 177Lu-PSMA-617 (7.4 GBq ±10% ×6) + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI (1:1, open-label); crossover 16%
endpoints: ✅ NR vs. NR (interim; 24% vs. 30% events) — HR 0.72 (0.58–0.90); P=0.0021
⏳ NR vs. NR (interim, immature) — HR 0.84 (0.63–1.13); P=0.13
takeaway: 177Lu-PSMA-617 added to ADT + ARPI improved rPFS in first-line mHSPC, the first phase 3 radioligand therapy trial in mHSPC. OS is immature, and there were more adverse events (dry mouth, cytopenias, GI) with HRQoL time-to-worsening HR ~1.1.

name: ABC-02
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer, PS 0–2, UK. ECOG 2 ~10%; metastatic ~75%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin (GemCis, GC) vs gemcitabine alone; up to 8 cycles (24 wks)
takeaway: Established GemCis as the standard of care in first-line advanced biliary tract cancer, beating gemcitabine alone on OS (HR 0.64) and PFS (HR 0.63).

name: ATHENA-MONO
population: FIGO stage III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer, regardless of HRD status. Complete response ~55%, stage III 76%, HRD 43%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (4:1), up to 2 years (maintenance)
endpoints: HRD-negative 12.1 vs. 9.1 — HR 0.65 (0.45–0.95); HR BRCAm 0.40; BRCA wt/LOH-high 0.58
Measurable disease only (~10%): ITT 48.8% vs. 9.1%; HRD 58.8% vs. 20.0% (not formally tested)
takeaway: First-line rucaparib maintenance after chemotherapy improved PFS in the HRD, ITT (HR 0.52) and HRD-negative (HR 0.65) populations. It covers the broadest first-line PARPi population (R0 allowed, 79% BRCA wild-type), though OS is still immature.

name: CABINET
population: Grade 1–3 NET with progression on at least one prior treatment (besides SSA) within 1 yr. Extrapancreatic NET (epNET) n=203 (GI 57%, lung 19%); pancreatic NET (pNET) n=95. ~60% prior Lu-177.
treatment: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1) in two cohorts (epNET, pNET); crossover allowed
takeaway: Cabozantinib improved PFS and ORR in both pancreatic and extrapancreatic NET after Lu-177/everolimus, but OS showed no benefit. OS is immature (trial stopped after the first interim) and crossover was 33–41%; dose reduction was needed in 60%.

name: EMERALD-3
population: Embolisation-eligible unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, no Vp3/Vp4; ≤1 prior palliative embolisation. BCLC A 20% / B 62% / C 18%; beyond up-to-7 62%; Asian 72%.
treatment: STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w) + lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + TACE vs STRIDE + TACE vs TACE alone (open-label, sponsor-blinded)
endpoints: STRIDE+TACE 12.9 vs. TACE (first 175) 8.1 — HR 0.71 (0.56–0.91) (descriptive, not formally tested)
STRIDE+TACE NR vs. 32.9 — HR 0.70 (0.51–0.95) (descriptive, not formally tested)
takeaway: STRIDE + lenvatinib + TACE improved PFS (13.0 vs 9.8, HR 0.70), but the OS HR of 0.84 was not significant at interim. STRIDE + TACE without lenvatinib looked as good (PFS HR 0.71, OS HR 0.70) with less toxicity, though that comparison was not formally tested; lenvatinib added G3–4 TRAEs, discontinuations and deaths.

name: FUGA-BT (JCOG1113)
population: Chemotherapy-naive BTC, PS 0–1, Japan. ECOG 1 26–31%; metastatic 60%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + S-1 (GS, given indefinitely) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GemCis; cisplatin ×8 cycles then gemcitabine); non-inferiority design
takeaway: Gemcitabine + S-1 was non-inferior to GemCis for OS in first-line BTC. It caused less haematologic toxicity but more mucosal toxicity.

name: HERIZON-GEA-01
population: Previously untreated HER2-positive (IHC3+ or IHC2+/ISH+) unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic gastric, GEJ or esophageal adenocarcinoma.
treatment: Zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemo vs zanidatamab + chemo vs trastuzumab + chemo (1:1:1)
takeaway: Both zanidatamab-containing regimens improved PFS over trastuzumab + chemo in first-line HER2+ advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. The tislelizumab triplet also improved OS at the first interim, while the zanidatamab + chemo OS result is not yet significant (further analyses planned); diarrhea is the dominant adverse event with zanidatamab-based regimens.

name: IMvigor011
population: MIBC after cystectomy, (y)pT2–4aN0 or (y)pT0–4aN+, no radiologic disease; ECOG 0–2. 761 enrolled in ctDNA surveillance (q6w ×9 mo + 1 yr); 250 ctDNA+ randomized (N+ 57%, T3/T4 72%).
treatment: Atezolizumab 1680 mg Q4W ×1 yr vs placebo (2:1), only if ctDNA+ on serial monitoring
takeaway: First prospective ctDNA-guided adjuvant RCT, showing both DFS and OS benefit, with OS benefit regardless of PD-L1. Patients with persistent ctDNA negativity had 2-yr DFS of 88% without treatment, which points toward de-escalation; follow-up is short (16.1 m).

name: LEAP-012
population: Unresectable, non-metastatic HCC amenable to TACE; no PVI or extrahepatic disease; Child-Pugh A. Excluded tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours, ≥50% of liver. BCLC A 31% / B 59% / C 10%; tumour burden score ≤6 48%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤2 yr) + TACE vs dual placebo + TACE; systemic therapy started 2–4 wk before first TACE
endpoints: ⚠️ Median not reported (interim); 24-mo OS 75% vs. 69% — HR 0.80 (0.57–1.11); P=0.087 (IA; boundary 0.0012)
takeaway: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab + TACE improved PFS (14.6 vs 10.0, HR 0.66), but OS, the dual primary endpoint, was not significant at interim and the trial was later closed for low likelihood of meeting the OS threshold. Toxicity was heavy, with G≥3 TRAE in 71%.

name: NCT01367002 (HER2+ USC)
population: HER2+ (IHC 3+ or 2+/FISH+) uterine serous carcinoma, stage III–IV after surgery (71%) or measurable recurrent (29%; PFI >6 mo, ≤3 prior ChT); ECOG 0–2. Central HER2 review; control arm older (median 73 vs. 66).
treatment: Carboplatin + paclitaxel (CP; AUC 5 + 175 mg/m2 q3w ×6) + trastuzumab (8 → 6 mg/kg q3w) then trastuzumab maintenance until PD vs CP alone
endpoints: Stage III–IV NR vs. 25.4 — HR 0.49 (0.25–0.97); recurrent 25.0 vs. 22.5 — HR 0.86 (0.36–2.10), NS (one-sided tests; 90% CIs)
takeaway: Adding trastuzumab to carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS (HR 0.46) and OS (HR 0.58) in HER2+ uterine serous carcinoma with no added toxicity. The benefit was largest in stage III–IV primary disease (OS NR vs 25.4) with no OS gain in recurrent disease; this is a small phase II (n=58) with one-sided α 0.10, closed early for slow accrual.

name: ABC-06
population: Advanced BTC with progression on 1L gemcitabine + cisplatin. ECOG 0-1. UK trial.
treatment: FOLFOX (up to 12 cycles) + active symptom control (ASC) vs ASC alone
endpoints: 4.0 mo (FOLFOX arm only; no routine imaging in ASC-alone arm)
takeaway: FOLFOX improved OS over active symptom control alone in 2L advanced BTC, making it the 2L standard of care. Caveat: the benefit is driven by the 6- and 12-month OS tail.

name: CLARINET
population: GEP-NET G1-2 (Ki-67 <10%), non-functioning, SSTR+. Pancreas 45%, midgut 36%; G1 ~70%; 96% stable disease at baseline; 84% treatment-naive.
treatment: Lanreotide 120 mg SC q28d vs placebo, up to 96 wk (24 doses)
takeaway: Lanreotide improved PFS over placebo in SSTR+, non-functioning G1-2 GI/pancreatic NET. The benefit came even though most patients had stable disease at baseline, supporting starting an SSA early. OS did not differ, with 46% crossover.

name: IMvigor130
population: Both cisplatin-eligible and -ineligible patients. Carboplatin 70% (A) / 66% (C); UTUC 27%. Arm B restricted to IC2/3 after Apr 2018.
treatment: Atezolizumab + platinum-gemcitabine (A) vs atezolizumab monotherapy (B) vs placebo + platinum-gemcitabine (C)
takeaway: Atezolizumab + chemotherapy improved PFS but final OS missed its boundary (HR 0.85). Atezolizumab monotherapy had OS about equal to chemo in ITT, with a signal only in PD-L1 IC2/3 cisplatin-ineligible patients (HR 0.56, post-hoc). In the cisplatin subgroup OS was 21.5 vs 13.4 (HR 0.76, exploratory), which supports a cisplatin-based ICI combination.

name: KEYNOTE-775
population: Advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer after 1 prior platinum (2 allowed if one was neo/adjuvant); no prior ICI or VEGF-targeted therapy; any histology except carcinosarcoma/sarcoma; ECOG 0–1. pMMR 84%; serous 26%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 20 mg QD + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (≤35 doses) vs treatment of physician's choice: doxorubicin 60 q3w or weekly paclitaxel 80 (3 on / 1 off)
takeaway: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab after platinum improved PFS, OS and ORR over doxorubicin/paclitaxel in endometrial cancer, including in pMMR disease (OS HR 0.68). Caveat: it is toxic, with grade ≥3 AEs in 89%, lenvatinib dose reduction in two-thirds and hypothyroidism in 57%.

name: LUMINOSITY
population: Advanced/metastatic c-Met protein-overexpressing (IHC ≥25% 3+), nonsquamous EGFR-wildtype NSCLC. ≤2 prior lines (≤1 prior cytotoxic chemo); ECOG 0-1; 98% prior platinum, 82% prior ICI.
treatment: Telisotuzumab vedotin (Teliso-V) monotherapy (single-arm)
endpoints: 5.7 (4.6–6.9) mo c-Met OE total; 5.5 (4.1–8.3) high; 6.0 (4.5–8.1) intermediate
14.5 (9.9–16.6) mo c-Met OE total; 14.6 high; 14.2 intermediate
takeaway: Telisotuzumab vedotin (c-Met-directed ADC, MMAE payload) gave an ORR of 28.6% (34.6% in c-Met high) in a heavily pretreated population (98% prior platinum, 82% prior ICI). It selects by protein expression (IHC), distinct from MET exon 14/amplification-driven approaches, giving a larger (~25%) eligible population. Squamous and EGFR-mutant cohorts closed for futility; the result supports an ongoing phase 3 vs docetaxel.

name: NETTER-1
population: G1-2 SSTR+ midgut NET with progression on standard octreotide LAR. Ileum 74%; liver metastases 83%; G1 69%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w ×4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in SSA-refractory midgut NET and is the standard of care. Caveats: OS was not significant, with 36% crossover, and adverse events include cytopenia and MDS.

name: PRIMA
population: High-risk FIGO III–IV HGSC/endometrioid, fallopian/peritoneal cancer, regardless of HRD status. Prior bevacizumab allowed. CR 70%, stage III 65%, HRD 51%; NACT 67%.
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1), up to 3 years; niraparib dose adjusted by body weight and platelets
takeaway: Niraparib maintenance after 1L adjuvant TC in high-risk ovarian cancer improved PFS regardless of HRD status, but OS did not improve. Caveat: grade ≥3 haematologic adverse events are high.

name: PSMAfore
population: Taxane-naive mCRPC with progression on 1 ARPI (abi/enza/daro/apa); 81% prior ARPI in the CRPC setting. Visceral metastases 13%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs switched ARPI (AAP or enzalutamide); 57% crossover
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS and time to SSE over a second ARPI switch in taxane-naive mCRPC, with OS no different. Caveat: OS is confounded by crossover (57%).

name: SOLO-1
population: FIGO III–IV HGSC/endometrioid, fallopian/peritoneal cancer with BRCA1/2 mutation. Prior bevacizumab excluded. CR 82%, stage III 83%, BRCA1 72%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1) up to 2 years (longer if PR)
takeaway: Olaparib maintenance after 1L adjuvant TC in BRCA-mutant ovarian cancer improved PFS, and the benefit was sustained after the 2-year stop. The OS result (HR 0.55) did not cross its significance boundary.

name: SUN1111
population: G1-2 pancreatic NET with progression within 1 yr. Prior chemotherapy 69%, prior SSA 36%; functioning (−) ~50%. No prior TKI/VEGF inhibitor.
treatment: Sunitinib 37.5 mg PO daily (continuous) vs placebo, both with BSC (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Sunitinib improved PFS and ORR in progressive pancreatic NET. Caveats: OS is immature, the trial stopped early because of toxicity in the placebo arm, and the benefit was shown only in pancreatic NET, not GI-NET.

name: TheraP
population: Post-docetaxel mCRPC; visceral metastases 7%; 90% prior ARPI.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs cabazitaxel (open-label); crossover 32% / 20%
endpoints: ✅ 5.1 vs 5.1 mo — HR 0.63 (0.46–0.86), P=0.0028; 1-yr PFS 19% vs 3% (benefit emerges after 6 mo)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved PSA response and PFS over cabazitaxel in post-docetaxel mCRPC, with OS no different. Caveats: OS is confounded by crossover, and side effects include thrombocytopenia (platelet decrease) and dry mouth.

name: ARIEL3
population: High-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer with CA-125 <ULN, enrolled regardless of HRD/BRCA status. BRCA-mutant 35%, HRD 63%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
endpoints: BRCAm 38% vs 9%; HRD 27% vs 7%; ITT 18% vs 8%
takeaway: Rucaparib improved PFS in platinum-sensitive 2L–3L ovarian cancer regardless of BRCA/HRD status, with the largest effect in BRCA-mutant disease. There was no OS benefit.

name: AtTEnd
population: Newly diagnosed residual/inoperable stage III–IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (no prior chemo for recurrence; prior adjuvant platinum OK if PFI ≥6 mo); carcinosarcoma allowed; ECOG 0–2. Recurrent 67%, Asian 20%, central dMMR 23%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg + carboplatin-paclitaxel q3w × 6–8 → atezolizumab until PD vs placebo + carboplatin-paclitaxel → placebo (2:1)
endpoints: ⚠️ 38.7 vs 30.2 mo — HR 0.82 (0.63–1.07); P=0.048 (boundary 0.024); interim, not significant
↔ No difference by MMR or PD-L1 status (data in appendix)
takeaway: Adding atezolizumab to chemotherapy in 1L endometrial cancer improved PFS, driven by dMMR (HR 0.36) with an overall HR of 0.74. There was no benefit in pMMR (PFS HR 0.92, OS HR 1.00), unlike RUBY, GY018 and DUO-E, and OS was an interim analysis that was not significant.

name: CARD
population: mCRPC with prior docetaxel (≥3 cycles) and prior ARSI (abiraterone or enzalutamide, with PD <12 mo). Prior ARPI: abiraterone 43%, enzalutamide 56%. Gleason ≥8 ~60%.
treatment: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² IV q3w vs alternative ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Cabazitaxel beat a switch to the alternative ARPI on ibPFS and OS in mCRPC after docetaxel and a first ARPI. It also confirms the poor efficacy of switching ARPI after early progression.

name: CREATE-X
population: HER2-negative stage I–IIIB breast cancer with residual disease (non-pCR) after neoadjuvant chemo, from Japan and South Korea. HR+ 68%, TNBC 32%; stage IIIA–IIIB ~40%.
treatment: Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 Q3W × 6–8 cycles + standard therapy vs standard therapy alone
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine for 6–8 cycles in HER2-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemo improved both DFS and OS. The benefit is concentrated in TNBC and was not significant in HR+ disease.

name: DUO-E
population: Newly diagnosed measurable stage III, stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (1L; prior adjuvant chemo allowed if relapse ≥12 mo); carcinosarcoma allowed. pMMR 80%, recurrent 52%, PD-L1+ (TAP ≥1%) ~67%.
treatment: Carboplatin-paclitaxel + durvalumab → durvalumab + olaparib vs CP + durvalumab → durvalumab vs CP + placebo (3 arms, 1:1:1)
endpoints: ⚠️ NR vs NR vs 25.9 mo (IA1, 28% maturity) — D+O HR 0.59 (0.42–0.83), P=0.003; D HR 0.77 (0.56–1.07), P=0.12; interim, not significant
takeaway: Durvalumab with chemotherapy, with or without olaparib, improved PFS in 1L endometrial cancer. Olaparib adds benefit mainly in pMMR (HR 0.76 vs durvalumab) and PD-L1+ disease and none in dMMR (HR 0.97), with little benefit in the PD-L1-negative subgroup; OS is immature.

name: ERA-223
population: Chemo-naive mCRPC with bone metastases, no visceral metastases; prior ARPi excluded.
treatment: Radium-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk × 6 + abiraterone/prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone (abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisone 5 mg BID)
takeaway: Adding radium-223 to abiraterone failed to improve SSE-free survival, and OS was numerically lower. It also increased fracture risk versus abiraterone alone, and the row notes that it is now contraindicated with abiraterone.

name: GOG-229E
population: Recurrent or persistent endometrial cancer after 1–2 prior cytotoxic regimens; measurable disease; GOG PS 0–2; no prior VEGF-targeted therapy. Serous 27%, grade 3 71%, 2 prior regimens 37%.
treatment: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w (single-arm, no control)
takeaway: Single-agent bevacizumab in 2L–3L endometrial cancer met its 6-mo PFS criterion (40%, best among GOG historical controls) but gave a modest ORR of 13.5%. Responses occurred across histologies (4/7 in serous), and high plasma VEGF-A was associated with no response and worse OS (exploratory).

name: KEYNOTE-868 (NRG-GY018)
population: Measurable stage III/IVA, or stage IVB / recurrent endometrial cancer (± measurable); prior adjuvant chemo allowed if ≥12 mo; carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG 0–2. Separate dMMR (n=225) and pMMR (n=591) cohorts.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin-paclitaxel × 6 → pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤14 cycles) vs placebo + CP → placebo
takeaway: Pembrolizumab with chemotherapy then pembrolizumab maintenance improved PFS in both cohorts of 1L advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (dMMR HR 0.30, pMMR HR 0.54), with no excess chemotherapy toxicity and irAEs as expected. OS is immature, and pMMR median follow-up was only 7.9 mo.

name: KEYNOTE-B15 / EV-304
population: Cisplatin-eligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2–T4aN0 or T1–T4aN1), ECOG 0–1. T3N0/T4aN0 ~72%; CPS ≥10 ~57%.
treatment: EV-P (neoadjuvant × 4 → surgery → adjuvant EV × 5 + P × 13) vs cisplatin-gemcitabine (neoadjuvant × 4) → surgery
takeaway: EV-P improved EFS, OS and pCR versus cisplatin-gemcitabine neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the first non-platinum regimen to beat cisplatin-based NAC. Together with KEYNOTE-905 it supports peri-operative EV-P regardless of cisplatin eligibility, though the control arm had no peri-operative ICI (cf. NIAGARA) and EV-P brought more AEs and longer treatment.

name: NETTER-2
population: Treatment-naive grade 2–3 SSTR+ GEP-NET. Pancreas 54%, small intestine 29%; G3 35%; liver metastases 90%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w × 4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w (2:1)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in 1L higher-grade GEP-NET. The ORR of 43% (CR 5%) is unusually high for NET, and OS is immature.

name: PACIFIC
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (IASLC 7th) without progression after ≥2 cycles of platinum chemoradiotherapy. Unselected for PD-L1 (TC ≥25% 22%, <25% 41%, unknown 37%); EGFR-mutant 6%.
treatment: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg Q2W up to 12 mo vs placebo (2:1); consolidation starting 1–42 days after chemoRT
takeaway: One year of consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiotherapy improved both PFS and OS and is SOC. Benefit was seen regardless of PD-L1 but was less in EGFR-mutant disease, and treatment should be started within 14 days after CRT.

name: PROMID
population: Treatment-naive grade 1–2 midgut NET. Ki-67 ≤2% in 95%; functional 39%; SSA scan positive 75%; hepatic tumor burden ≤10% ~75%.
treatment: Octreotide LAR 30 mg IM q28d vs placebo, until PFS event (N = 85)
takeaway: Octreotide LAR prolonged time to progression in 1L functioning and non-functioning midgut NET and is SOC. As the very first SSA trial, it showed an anti-proliferative effect and not just symptom control.

name: RADIANT-2
population: Grade 1–2 functioning GI-NET with progression within 1 yr. Small intestine 52%, lung 10%, colon 7%; prior SSA 79%; prior chemo 30%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily + octreotide LAR 30 mg q28d vs placebo + octreotide LAR 30 mg q28d
