takeaway: Everolimus added to octreotide in functioning GI-NET missed the PFS boundary, with OS showing no difference. This led on to RADIANT-4 in non-functioning NETs.

name: SOLO-2
population: High-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer with germline BRCA mutation.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Olaparib improved PFS in germline BRCA-mutant relapsed ovarian cancer. OS was not significant but became significant when adjusted for the 38% crossover, and MDS/AML occurred in 8% with long exposure.

name: CARES-005
population: Unresectable HCC treatable with TACE (CNLC Ib–IIIa = BCLC A–C without extrahepatic mets), Child-Pugh A; China only. BCLC C 43%, PVTT Vp3–4 27%, beyond up-to-7 90%, HBV 80%.
treatment: TACE + camrelizumab 200 mg q3w + rivoceranib (apatinib) 250 mg QD vs TACE alone (on-demand cTACE; crossover allowed at progression)
endpoints: ✅ Composite (RECICL + CP-C + TACE failure/refractoriness) 10.8 vs 3.2 — HR 0.34 (0.24–0.50), P<0.001
⏳ 24.0 vs 21.5 — HR 0.87 (0.57–1.32), P=0.50; immature (90 deaths), 75% of TACE-arm progressors crossed over
takeaway: Adding camrelizumab + rivoceranib to TACE lifted PFS from 3.2 to 10.8 (HR 0.34), and it is the only TACE-combination trial here that enrolled BCLC C / Vp3–4 PVTT (27%). OS is immature and confounded by 75% crossover, and this is a phase II, open-label, investigator-assessed, China-only trial.

name: GOG0209
population: Chemo-naive stage III/IV or recurrent endometrial cancer with poor potential for cure by surgery/RT; GOG PS 0–2. Measurable or recurrent disease 61%; non-measurable stage III/IV allowed from 2006.
treatment: Paclitaxel 175 + carboplatin AUC 6 (TC) q3w ×7 vs TAP (doxorubicin 45 + cisplatin 50 d1, paclitaxel 160 d2 + G-CSF) q3w ×7
takeaway: Carboplatin + paclitaxel was non-inferior to TAP for OS and PFS, with less toxicity and slightly better QoL. TC became the 1L standard for advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer and the backbone for later ICI trials (GY018, RUBY, DUO-E).

name: KEYNOTE-966
population: Treatment-naive advanced BTC, ECOG PS 0–1, global enrolment. ECOG 0 43–48%; iCCA 60%; metastatic ~90%; PD-L1 (+) ~70%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + gemcitabine–cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine–cisplatin; maintenance gem-pembro
takeaway: Adding pembrolizumab to gemcitabine–cisplatin improved OS in 1L advanced BTC, but the PFS result did not meet its significance threshold (P=0.023 vs 0.0125) and ORR was identical between arms.

name: NIFTY
population: Metastatic BTC with progression on 1L gemcitabine–cisplatin; ECOG 0–1; South Korea.
treatment: Liposomal irinotecan + 5-FU/LV vs 5-FU/LV alone; chemotherapy indefinite
takeaway: Liposomal irinotecan added to 5-FU/LV improved PFS and OS over 5-FU/LV alone in 2L metastatic BTC. It is a phase II trial from South Korea, and the ORR difference was not significant (P=0.068).

name: RADIANT-3
population: G1–2 pancreatic NET with progression within 1 yr. Well differentiated 83%; liver mets 92%; functional 24%; prior chemo 50%, prior SSA 49%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo, both with best supportive care (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in progressive pNET and became the standard in 2L. Most disease stabilized rather than responded (ORR 5%), OS was not different with 73% crossover, and adverse effects include stomatitis, hyperglycemia and ILD.

name: TAX 327
population: mCRPC with progression on ADT; chemo-naive; ~90% bone mets.
treatment: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² Q3W (D3P) vs docetaxel 30 mg/m² QW (D1P) vs mitoxantrone Q3W (MP), all + prednisolone 5 mg BID
takeaway: Docetaxel q3w + prednisone (D3P) improved OS, pain, PSA and QoL over mitoxantrone in mCRPC. Weekly docetaxel (D1P) did not improve OS, so D3P became the standard.

name: VISION
population: mCRPC after ≥1 ARPI and 1–2 taxanes; visceral ~20%; 38% prior cabazitaxel; 40% 2 prior ARPIs. PSMA-PET-selected.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 + SOC vs SOC (excludes ChT, other RLT, IO); 2:1
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS and OS over SOC in post-taxane, post-ARPI, PSMA-PET-selected mCRPC, and led to FDA approval.

name: ALSYMPCA
population: Symptomatic mCRPC with bone metastases and no visceral metastases (bone only). Had received, were ineligible for, or declined docetaxel (57% prior docetaxel); >20 metastases in 30%.
treatment: Radium-223 vs placebo (+ BSC) — Ra-223 50 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6
endpoints: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event
takeaway: Radium-223 improved overall survival and delayed the first symptomatic skeletal event versus placebo plus BSC in symptomatic mCRPC with bone-only metastases. It was the first overall survival benefit from a bone-targeted radiopharmaceutical.

name: BILCAP
population: Resected (R0/R1) biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder), ECOG <2 (ECOG 1 ~50%). Stage II 60%.
treatment: Capecitabine 24 wk vs observation — capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 q3w
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine showed an OS benefit in the per-protocol and adjusted sensitivity analyses, which led to its use as standard of care. However, the primary ITT OS analysis was not significant (P=0.097), and the RFS benefit appeared only during capecitabine treatment, with recurrences occurring after the 24 weeks.

name: ClarIDHy
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment; IDH1 mutation.
treatment: Ivosidenib vs placebo (2:1); crossover 57%
takeaway: Ivosidenib improved PFS versus placebo in IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma after at least one prior treatment. ITT OS was not significant because of 57% crossover, while the RPSFT crossover-adjusted analysis showed an OS benefit.

name: ECOG-ACRIN E2211
population: Advanced/unresectable pancreatic NET, low/intermediate grade, with radiographic progression within 12 mo. No prior temozolomide, DTIC, capecitabine or 5-FU; prior SSA 63%, everolimus ~35%, sunitinib ~10%; liver metastases 94%.
treatment: CAPTEM (capecitabine 750 mg/m² BID D1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² D10–14, q28d) vs temozolomide alone (200 mg/m² D1–5, q28d), up to 13 cycles
takeaway: This is the only randomized trial of CAPTEM in pancreatic NET: adding capecitabine lengthened PFS (22.7 vs 14.4, HR 0.58) with the highest ORR (~40%) of any randomized pNET regimen. The OS gain (~5 mo) was not significant and toxicity doubled (Gr3–4 45% vs 22%). MGMT deficiency predicted response (IHC-low ORR 52% vs 15%), so test it when shrinkage is the goal.

name: FIGHT-202
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment; FGFR2 fusion. Other FGFR2 alterations enrolled as comparator cohorts.
treatment: Pemigatinib (pan-FGFR1–3 TKI) monotherapy, single-arm
endpoints: ✅ FGFR2 fusion 35.5% vs 0% in both other cohorts
takeaway: Pemigatinib produced a 35.5% ORR in second-line or later FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma, with PFS and OS favorable versus chemotherapy historical control. Caveats: 0% ORR in other FGF/FGFR alterations, and a class adverse event of hyperphosphatemia.

name: KHBO1401-MITSUBA
population: Advanced BTC; adjuvant chemotherapy ≥6 mo allowed. PS 0–2 (no PS 2 in GCS arm). Japan. Metastatic 50%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin + S-1 (GCS) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC); both 24 wk
takeaway: Adding S-1 to gemcitabine-cisplatin improved PFS, OS and ORR in first-line advanced BTC in a Japanese population. The primary OS hazard ratio is reported with a 90% CI.

name: LAURA
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (AJCC 8th) with EGFR Ex19del or L858R, no progression after platinum-based chemoradiotherapy. Asian 82%; L858R 41–48%.
treatment: Osimertinib 80 mg QD vs placebo (2:1) until PD; crossover allowed
takeaway: Osimertinib after chemoradiotherapy greatly improved PFS in EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III NSCLC, so test EGFR before chemoRT. OS is immature (20% maturity) and confounded by 81% crossover.

name: MITO END-2
population: Advanced (FIGO III–IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, measurable or evaluable; ≤1 prior platinum line (≥6 mo interval); carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG ≤2. Recurrent ~62%, G3 ~50%, serous/clear cell 16%, prior chemotherapy 24%.
treatment: Carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 q3w ×6–8 (CP) + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab maintenance vs CP alone
endpoints: ❌ 13.7 vs 10.5 — HR 0.84 (0.5–1.3), P=0.43 (log-rank NS); post-hoc Breslow P=0.08 (study α 0.20)
takeaway: Adding bevacizumab to carboplatin-paclitaxel in advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer did not meet the primary PFS endpoint, though ORR, 6-month DCR and OS were numerically higher. Caveats: more thromboembolism, hypertension and discontinuations, and this was a small phase II without molecular stratification.

name: RADIANT-4
population: Nonfunctioning G1–2 GI or lung NET: lung 30%, GI 58%, unknown primary 12%. Prior SSA >50%; prior chemotherapy ~25%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1), both with best supportive care
takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in nonfunctioning GI/lung NET, and became standard of care as second-line therapy. OS showed a trend that was not significant at the first interim analysis.

name: RUBY
population: Primary advanced stage III–IV (not amenable to cure) or first recurrent endometrial cancer; carcinosarcoma allowed. dMMR/MSI-H 24%; recurrent 48%, primary stage IV 34%, stage III 19%.
treatment: Dostarlimab 500 mg + carboplatin-paclitaxel q3w ×6 → dostarlimab 1000 mg q6w (≤3 yr) vs placebo + carboplatin-paclitaxel → placebo
takeaway: Dostarlimab with carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS in first-line advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer, with the largest effect in dMMR (HR 0.28; 24-mo PFS 61% vs 16%) and a smaller benefit in pMMR (PFS HR 0.76). OS was favorable (HR 0.64) but interim, and the boundary was not crossed.

name: VISION
population: mNSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping mutation (liquid and/or tissue biopsy); ≤2 prior lines; ECOG 0–1. Stable/treated brain metastases 11%.
treatment: Tepotinib monotherapy, single-arm
takeaway: Tepotinib produced a 46% ORR in MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC. A class adverse event to note is peripheral edema.

name: AMPLITUDE
population: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) with HRD required. BRCA1/2 56%, high volume 78%, prior docetaxel 16%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg + abiraterone 1000 mg (dual-action tablet) + prednisone 5 mg QD vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone
takeaway: Niraparib plus abiraterone improved rPFS over abiraterone alone in HRR-altered mCSPC, while OS is still immature. Benefit is concentrated in BRCA patients (non-BRCA HRD HR 0.81, post hoc), and anemia and hypertension were the adverse events flagged.

name: EMERALD-1
population: Unresectable HCC amenable to TACE, no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A–B7; Vp3/Vp4 excluded. BCLC A 26% / B 57% / C 16%. Beyond up-to-7 criteria 52%; PVI (Vp1–2) 7%.
treatment: TACE + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w, then durvalumab 1120 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w (bevacizumab only ≥14 d after last TACE) vs TACE + durvalumab + placebo vs TACE + placebo
endpoints: ⏳ Not reported (interim OS not significant; still masked)
takeaway: This was the first positive phase 3 of systemic therapy plus TACE, with durvalumab + bevacizumab + TACE giving PFS 15.0 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.77). Durvalumab alone with TACE did not help, so the anti-VEGF partner matters, and OS is not yet reported.

name: FOENIX-CCA2
population: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion and ≥1 prior treatment; 57% had ≥2 prior treatments.
treatment: Futibatinib monotherapy (single-arm); irreversible pan-FGFR1-4 TKI
takeaway: Futibatinib produced a 42% ORR in previously treated FGFR2 fusion intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, treated in second line or later. It is a single-arm study with no comparator.

name: IMvigor010
population: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (bladder 93%, UTUC 7%) after radical surgery + LND: ypT2–4a/ypN+ post-NAC, or pT3–4a/pN+ without NAC (cisplatin-ineligible or declined). pN+ 52%; prior NAC 48%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W ×1 yr vs observation
takeaway: The first phase 3 adjuvant ICI trial in MIUC was negative for both DFS and OS, with no benefit by PD-L1. In the exploratory ctDNA+ group (37%) atezolizumab improved OS (HR 0.59), whereas ctDNA− patients had no benefit and more AEs, a finding that was then tested prospectively in IMvigor011.

name: KEYNOTE-158
population: MSI-H/dMMR non-CRC solid tumours, progressed on ≥1 prior treatment. Cholangiocarcinoma n=22 (9.4%).
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy (single-arm)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab gave a 34.3% ORR in previously treated MSI-H/dMMR cancers, including 40.9% in cholangiocarcinoma, with OS better than a chemotherapy historical control. The FDA approval is tissue-agnostic for dMMR/MSI-H cancers.

name: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16)
population: Predominantly high-grade serous carcinoma. Two cohorts: gBRCA (n=203) and non-gBRCA (n=350), the latter tested for HRD (myChoice).
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Niraparib improved PFS in second-line gBRCA (HR 0.27) and non-gBRCA (HR 0.45) patients, but there was no OS benefit. Grade ≥3 thrombocytopenia occurred in 34%.

name: PEACE-3
population: First-line mCRPC with bone metastases and no visceral metastases. 30% prior docetaxel.
treatment: Radium-223 + enzalutamide vs enzalutamide (open-label). Enzalutamide 160 mg/d; Ra-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6; bone-protecting agent mandatory
endpoints: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event
takeaway: Radium-223 added to enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS over enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC. A bone-protecting agent is mandatory, and fracture and ONJ risk is higher than with enzalutamide alone.

name: TOPAZ-1
population: Treatment-naive advanced BTC, ECOG PS 0–1, global. ECOG 0 ~50%; iCCA ~55%; metastatic ~90%; PD-L1 positive ~60%.
treatment: Durvalumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine/cisplatin; no maintenance gemcitabine
takeaway: Durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin improved PFS, OS and ORR over chemotherapy alone in first-line advanced BTC and is the standard of care.
